verses.1:1: And King David had grown old and had very many days of age; and although he was covered with garments, he did not grow warm.
verses.1:2: Therefore his servants said to him, "Let us seek a young woman, a virgin, for our lord the king, and let her stand before the king and care for him, and let her sleep in his bosom and warm our lord the king."
verses.1:3: So they sought a lovely young woman throughout all the borders of Israel, and they found Abishag the Shunammite, and brought her to the king.
verses.1:4: Now the girl was exceedingly beautiful, and she slept with the king and served him; however, the king did not know her.
verses.1:5: Now Adonijah the son of Haggith was exalting himself, saying, "I will reign." And he prepared for himself chariots and horsemen, and fifty men to run before him.
verses.1:6: Nor did his father ever reprove him, saying, "Why have you done this?" Moreover, he himself was also very handsome, second by birth after Absalom.
verses.1:7: And he had discussion with Joab the son of Zeruiah and with Abiathar the priest, who were supporting the side of Adonijah.
verses.1:8: But Zadok the priest, and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, and Nathan the prophet, and Shimei and Rei, and the strength of David's army were not with Adonijah.
verses.1:9: Therefore Adonijah, having sacrificed rams and calves and all the fattened beasts beside the stone of Zoheleth, which was near the spring of Rogel, called all his brothers, the sons of the king, and all the men of Judah, the servants of the king.
verses.1:10: But Nathan the prophet, and Benaiah, and all the strong men, and Solomon his brother he did not call.
verses.1:11: So Nathan said to Bathsheba the mother of Solomon, "Have you heard that Adonijah the son of Haggith has begun to reign, and our lord David does not know this?
verses.1:12: Now therefore come, take counsel from me, and save your life and the life of your son Solomon.
verses.1:13: Go, and go in to King David, and say to him, 'Did you not, my lord the king, swear to me your maidservant, saying, "Solomon your son will reign after me, and he himself will sit on my throne"? Why then is Adonijah reigning?'
verses.1:14: And while you are still speaking there with the king, I will come after you and complete your words."
verses.1:15: So Bathsheba went in to the king in the bedchamber; now the king had grown exceedingly old, and Abishag the Shunammite was serving him.
verses.1:16: Bathsheba bowed down and paid homage to the king. To her the king said, "What do you want?"
verses.1:17: She answered and said, "My lord, you swore by the Lord your God to your maidservant, 'Solomon your son will reign after me, and he himself will sit on my throne.'
verses.1:18: And look, now Adonijah is reigning, while you, my lord the king, do not know it.
verses.1:19: He has slaughtered oxen, and all the fattened beasts, and very many rams, and has called all the sons of the king, Abiathar the priest also, and Joab the commander of the forces; but Solomon your servant he has not called.
verses.1:20: However, my lord the king, the eyes of all Israel are looking toward you, that you may declare to them who ought to sit on your throne, my lord the king, after you.
verses.1:21: And it will be that when my lord the king sleeps with his fathers, I and my son Solomon will be sinners."
verses.1:22: While she was still speaking with the king, Nathan the prophet came.
verses.1:23: And they announced to the king, saying, "Nathan the prophet is here." And when he had entered into the presence of the king and had paid homage to him, face down to the ground,
verses.1:24: Nathan said, "My lord the king, have you said, 'Adonijah shall reign after me, and he himself shall sit upon my throne'?
verses.1:25: For he has gone down today, and has sacrificed oxen, and fattened beasts, and very many rams, and has called all the sons of the king and the commanders of the army, and Abiathar the priest also; and while they are eating and drinking before him and saying, 'May King Adonijah live,'
verses.1:26: me your servant, and Zadok the priest, and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, and Solomon your servant he has not called.
verses.1:27: Has this word come out from my lord the king, and have you not declared to me, your servant, who was going to sit upon the throne of my lord the king after him?"
verses.1:28: And King David answered, saying, "Call Bathsheba to me." And when she had gone in before the king and had stood before him,
verses.1:29: the king swore and said, "As the Lord lives, who has delivered my life from every distress,
verses.1:30: surely, just as I swore to you by the Lord God of Israel, saying, 'Solomon your son will reign after me, and he himself will sit upon my throne in my place,' so I will do today."
verses.1:31: And Bathsheba, having lowered her face to the ground, paid homage to the king, saying, "May my lord David live forever."
verses.1:32: King David also said, "Call to me Zadok the priest, and Nathan the prophet, and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada." And when they had gone in before the king,
verses.1:33: he said to them, "Take with you the servants of your lord, and set my son Solomon upon my mule, and lead him to Gihon.
verses.1:34: And let Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet anoint him there as king over Israel; and you will sound the trumpet and say, 'May King Solomon live!'
verses.1:35: And you will come up after him, and he will come and sit upon my throne, and he himself will reign in my place; and I will command him to be leader over Israel and over Judah."
verses.1:36: And Benaiah the son of Jehoiada answered the king, saying, "Amen! So may the Lord God of my lord the king speak.
verses.1:37: Just as the Lord was with my lord the king, so may He be with Solomon, and may He make his throne higher than the throne of my lord King David."
verses.1:38: Therefore Zadok the priest, and Nathan the prophet, and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, and the Cherethites, and the Pelethites went down; and they set Solomon upon the mule of King David and brought him to Gihon.
verses.1:39: And Zadok the priest took the horn of oil from the tabernacle and anointed Solomon; and they sounded the trumpet, and all the people said, "May King Solomon live!"
verses.1:40: And the entire multitude went up after him, and the people, playing flutes and rejoicing with great joy; and the earth resounded from their outcry.
verses.1:41: Now Adonijah and all who had been invited by him heard it, and the banquet was already finished; and Joab also, having heard the sound of the trumpet, said, "What does the outcry of the city in tumult mean?"
verses.1:42: While he was still speaking, Jonathan the son of Abiathar the priest came; to whom Adonijah said, "Come in, for you are a valiant man and bringing good news."
verses.1:43: And Jonathan answered Adonijah, "By no means! For our lord King David has appointed Solomon as king;
verses.1:44: and he sent with him Zadok the priest, and Nathan the prophet, and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, and the Cherethites, and the Pelethites, and they set him upon the king's mule.
verses.1:45: And Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet anointed him king in Gihon; and they came up from there rejoicing, and the city resounded; this is the sound that you heard.
verses.1:46: And moreover, Solomon is sitting upon the throne of the kingdom.
verses.1:47: And the servants of the king went in and blessed our lord King David, saying, 'May God enlarge the name of Solomon above your name, and make his throne great above your throne.' And the king worshiped on his bed,
verses.1:48: and spoke, 'Blessed be the Lord God of Israel, who has given today one sitting on my throne, while my eyes see it.'"
verses.1:49: Therefore all who had been invited by Adonijah were terrified and rose up, and each one went on his way.
verses.1:50: Now Adonijah, fearing Solomon, rose up and went away, and took hold of the horn of the altar.
verses.1:51: And they announced to Solomon, saying, "Look, Adonijah, fearing King Solomon, has taken hold of the horn of the altar, saying, 'Let King Solomon swear to me today that he will not kill his servant with the sword.'"
verses.1:52: And Solomon said, "If he is a good man, not even a single hair of his will fall to the ground; but if evil is found in him, he will die."
verses.1:53: Therefore King Solomon sent and brought him out from the altar; and having come in, he paid homage to King Solomon; and Solomon said to him, "Go to your house."
verses.2:1: Now the days drew near for David to die, and he commanded Solomon his son, saying:
verses.2:2: "I am entering the way of all the earth; be strong, and be a man.
verses.2:3: And observe the charges of the Lord your God, to walk in His ways, to keep His ceremonies, and His commands, and judgments, and testimonies, as it is written in the law of Moses, so that you may understand all that you do, and wherever you turn,
verses.2:4: so that the Lord may confirm His words which He spoke concerning me, saying, 'If your sons keep their ways, and walk before Me in truth, with all their heart and with all their soul, no man will be removed from you from the throne of Israel.'
verses.2:5: You also know what Joab the son of Zeruiah did to me, what he did to the two commanders of the army of Israel, Abner the son of Ner and Amasa the son of Jether, whom he killed, and shed the blood of war in peace, and put the blood of battle on his belt that was around his waist and on his footwear that was on his feet.
verses.2:6: Therefore you will act according to your wisdom, and you will not bring his gray hair down peacefully to the underworld.
verses.2:7: But to the sons of Barzillai the Gileadite also you will return kindness, and they will be eating at your table; for they came to meet me when I was fleeing from the face of Absalom your brother.
verses.2:8: You also have with you Shimei the son of Gera, the son of Jemini, from Bahurim, who cursed me with a very wicked curse when I was going to the camp; but because he came down to meet me when I was crossing the Jordan, and I swore to him by the Lord, saying, 'I will not put you to death with the sword,'
verses.2:9: you must not allow him to go unpunished. Now you are a wise man, so that you know what you will do to him, and you will bring his gray hairs down with blood to the underworld."
verses.2:10: So David slept with his fathers, and was buried in the city of David.
verses.2:11: Now the days in which David reigned over Israel are forty years: in Hebron he reigned seven years; in Jerusalem, thirty-three.
verses.2:12: And Solomon sat on the throne of David his father, and his kingdom was made exceedingly firm.
verses.2:13: And Adonijah the son of Haggith came in to Bathsheba the mother of Solomon. And she said to him, "Is your coming peaceful?" And he answered, "Peaceful."
verses.2:14: And he added, "I have a word for you." To him she said, "Speak." And he replied:
verses.2:15: "You," he said, "know that the kingdom was mine, and all Israel had set me over themselves as king; yet the kingdom has been transferred and has become my brother's, for it was appointed to him by the Lord.
verses.2:16: Now therefore I ask one request of you: do not put my face to shame." And she said to him, "Speak."
verses.2:17: And he said, "I beg that you speak to King Solomon (for he cannot deny you anything) that he give me Abishag the Shunammite as a wife."
verses.2:18: And Bathsheba said, "Very well; I will speak for you to the king."
verses.2:19: So Bathsheba came to King Solomon to speak to him for Adonijah; and the king rose to meet her, and bowed down to her, and sat on his throne; and a throne was set for the king's mother, who sat at his right hand.
verses.2:20: And she said to him, "One little request I ask of you: do not put my face to shame." And the king said to her, "Ask, my mother, for it is not right that I should turn away your face."
verses.2:21: And she said, "Let Abishag the Shunammite be given to Adonijah your brother as a wife."
verses.2:22: And King Solomon answered and said to his mother, "Why do you ask for Abishag the Shunammite for Adonijah? Ask for the kingdom for him as well, for he is my brother older than I, and he has Abiathar the priest and Joab the son of Zeruiah."
verses.2:23: Therefore King Solomon swore by the Lord, saying, "May God do these things to me, and add these things, for Adonijah has spoken this word against his own life.
verses.2:24: And now, as the Lord lives, who has established me and set me on the throne of David my father, and who has made a house for me as He spoke, today Adonijah will be killed."
verses.2:25: And King Solomon sent by the hand of Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, who put him to death, and he died.
verses.2:26: The king also said to Abiathar the priest, "Go to Anathoth, to your field; indeed you are a man of death, but today I will not put you to death, because you carried the ark of the Lord God before David my father, and you endured toil in all things in which my father toiled."
verses.2:27: So Solomon cast out Abiathar, that he might not be priest of the Lord, so that the word of the Lord might be fulfilled which He spoke concerning the house of Eli in Shiloh.
verses.2:28: Now a report came to Joab, for Joab had turned aside after Adonijah, and had not turned aside after Solomon; therefore Joab fled into the tabernacle of the Lord, and took hold of the horn of the altar.
verses.2:29: And it was reported to King Solomon that Joab had fled into the tabernacle of the Lord and was beside the altar; and Solomon sent Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, saying, "Go, put him to death."
verses.2:30: And Benaiah came to the tabernacle of the Lord and said to him, "This is what the king says: 'Come out.'" And he said, "I will not come out, but I will die here." Benaiah reported the word back to the king, saying, "This is what Joab spoke, and this is what he answered me."
verses.2:31: And the king said to him, "Do as he has spoken, and put him to death, and bury him; and you will remove the innocent blood that was shed by Joab from me and from the house of my father.
verses.2:32: And the Lord will return his blood upon his head, because he killed two righteous men, better than himself, and cut them down with the sword, while my father David was unaware, Abner the son of Ner, commander of the forces of Israel, and Amasa the son of Jether, commander of the army of Judah;
verses.2:33: and their blood will return upon the head of Joab and upon the head of his offspring forever. But for David, and for his offspring, and for his house, and for his throne, may there be peace to all eternity from the Lord."
verses.2:34: So Benaiah the son of Jehoiada went up, and attacking him, put him to death; and he was buried in his house in the wilderness.
verses.2:35: And the king appointed Benaiah the son of Jehoiada in his place over the army, and he set Zadok the priest in place of Abiathar. Now the chief officers set over all the works of Solomon were five hundred and fifty, who had the people subject to them and directed the appointed works. Solomon also offered, three times each year, burnt offerings and peace sacrifices on the altar that he had built for the Lord, and burned incense before the Lord; and the temple was completed.
verses.2:36: The king also sent and summoned Shimei, and said to him, "Build a house for yourself in Jerusalem, and live there; and you will not go out from there this way or that.
verses.2:37: Now on whatever day you go out, and cross the brook Kidron, know that you are to be put to death; your blood will be upon your head."
verses.2:38: And Shimei said to the king, "The word is good; just as my lord the king has spoken, so your servant will do." So Shimei lived in Jerusalem for many days.
verses.2:39: Now it happened after three years that servants of Shimei fled to Achish the son of Maacah, king of Gath; and it was reported to Shimei that his servants had gone to Gath.
verses.2:40: And Shimei rose, and saddled his donkey, and went to Achish in Gath to search for his servants, and brought them from Gath.
verses.2:41: Now it was reported to Solomon that Shimei had gone to Gath from Jerusalem and had returned.
verses.2:42: And he sent and summoned him, and said to him, "Did I not solemnly warn you by the Lord, and tell you beforehand, 'On whatever day you leave and go this way and that, know that you are going to die,' and you answered me, 'The word that I have heard is good'?
verses.2:43: Why then did you not keep the oath of the Lord, and the command that I had commanded you?"
verses.2:44: And the king said to Shimei, "You know all the evil of which your heart is conscious within you, which you did to David my father; the Lord has returned your wickedness upon your head;
verses.2:45: and King Solomon is blessed, and the throne of David will be steadfast before the Lord forever."
verses.2:46: So the king ordered Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, who went out and struck him, and he died. Judah and Israel were innumerable, like the sand of the sea in multitude, eating, and drinking, and rejoicing. Now Solomon was in his dominion, having all the kingdoms from the river of the land of the Philistines to the border of Egypt, who were offering him gifts and serving him all the days of his life. And Judah and Israel lived without any fear, each one under his vine and under his fig tree, from Dan to Beersheba, all the days of Solomon.
verses.3:2: However, the people were sacrificing on the high places, for a temple had not been built for the name of the Lord until that day.
verses.3:3: Now Solomon loved the Lord, walking in the precepts of David his father, except that he was sacrificing on the high places and burning incense.
verses.3:4: So he went to Gibeon to sacrifice there, for that was the greatest high place. Solomon offered a thousand sacrifices as a burnt offering on that altar in Gibeon.
verses.3:5: Now the Lord appeared to Solomon through a dream at night, saying, "Ask what you want Me to give you."
verses.3:6: And Solomon said, "You have shown great mercy to Your servant David my father, just as he walked in Your sight in truth and righteousness and with an upright heart toward You. You have kept Your great mercy for him, and You have given him a son sitting on his throne, as it is today.
verses.3:7: And now, Lord God, You have made Your servant reign in place of David my father, yet I am a little child and do not know my going out and my coming in.
verses.3:8: And Your servant is in the midst of the people whom You have chosen, a boundless people who cannot be numbered or reckoned because of their multitude.
verses.3:9: Therefore give Your servant a teachable heart, so that he may be able to judge Your people and discern between good and evil. For who will be able to judge this people, this numerous people of Yours?"
verses.3:10: Therefore the word was pleasing before the Lord, that Solomon had asked for such a thing.
verses.3:11: And the Lord said to Solomon, "Because you have asked for this matter, and have not sought for yourself many days, nor riches, nor the lives of your enemies, but have asked for yourself wisdom to discern justice,
verses.3:12: look, I have done for you according to your words, and I have given you a wise and understanding heart, to such an extent that no one like you has existed before you, nor will arise after you.
verses.3:13: Moreover, I have also given you these things that you did not ask for: namely, riches and glory, so that no one among the kings has been like you in all past days.
verses.3:14: And if you walk in My ways, and keep My precepts and My commandments, just as your father walked, I will make your days long."
verses.3:15: Therefore Solomon awoke and realized that it was a dream. And when he had come to Jerusalem, he stood before the ark of the covenant of the Lord, and offered burnt offerings, and made peace offerings and a great banquet for all his servants.
verses.3:16: Then two prostitute women came to the king and stood before him.
verses.3:17: One of them said, "I implore you, my lord: I and this woman were living in one house, and I gave birth with her in the bedroom.
verses.3:18: And on the third day after I gave birth, this woman also gave birth; and we were together, and no one else was with us in the house except the two of us.
verses.3:19: Now the son of this woman died during the night, for while sleeping she crushed him.
verses.3:20: And rising up in the silence of the dead of night, she took my son from my side while your maidservant was sleeping, and placed him in her bosom; but her own son, who was dead, she laid in my bosom.
verses.3:21: And when I had risen in the morning to give milk to my son, he appeared dead. Looking at him more closely in the clear light, I discovered that he was not my own whom I had borne."
verses.3:22: And the other woman answered, "It is not as you say, but your son is dead, and mine is alive." On the contrary, the first kept saying, "You are lying! For my son is alive, and your son is dead." And in this manner they were arguing before the king.
verses.3:23: Then the king said, "This one says, 'My son is alive, and your son is dead,' and that one replied, 'No, rather your son is dead, and mine is alive.'"
verses.3:24: Therefore the king said, "Bring me a sword." And when they had brought a sword before the king,
verses.3:25: he said, "Divide the living infant into two parts, and give half to the one and half to the other."
verses.3:26: Now the woman whose son was alive said to the king (for her innermost being was moved over her son), "I implore you, lord, give her the living infant, and do not kill him." On the contrary, the other was saying, "Let him be neither mine nor yours, but let him be divided."
verses.3:27: The king answered and said, "Give this woman the living infant, and let him not be put to death, for she is his mother."
verses.3:28: So all Israel heard the judgment that the king had judged, and they feared the king, seeing that the wisdom of God was in him to do justice.
verses.4:1: Now King Solomon was reigning over all Israel.
verses.4:2: And these were the officials whom he had: Azariah the son of Zadok the priest;
verses.4:3: Elihoreph and Ahijah, the sons of Shisha, were scribes; Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud was keeper of the records;
verses.4:4: Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was over the army; and Zadok and Abiathar were priests;
verses.4:5: Azariah the son of Nathan was over those who attended the king; Zabud the son of Nathan was priest, the friend of the king;
verses.4:6: and Ahishar was overseer of the household; and Adoniram the son of Abda was over the tributes.
verses.4:7: Now Solomon had twelve prefects over all Israel, who furnished provisions for the king and his household; for during each month of the year, each one supplied the necessities.
verses.4:8: And these were their names: Ben-hur, in the hill country of Ephraim.
verses.4:9: Ben-deker, in Makaz, and in Shaalbim, and in Beth-shemesh, and in Elon, and in Beth-hanan.
verses.4:10: Ben-hesed, in Arubboth; to him belonged Socoh and all the land of Hepher.
verses.4:11: Ben-abinadab, to whom belonged all Naphath-dor; he had Taphath, the daughter of Solomon, as his wife.
verses.4:12: Baana the son of Ahilud governed Taanach and Megiddo, and all Beth-shean, which is beside Zarethan below Jezreel, from Beth-shean as far as Abel-meholah, opposite Jokmeam.
verses.4:13: Ben-geber, in Ramoth-gilead; he had Havvoth-jair of the son of Manasseh in Gilead; he himself presided in all the region of Argob, which is in Bashan, over sixty great and walled cities that had bronze bars.
verses.4:14: Ahinadab the son of Iddo presided in Mahanaim.
verses.4:15: Ahimaaz, in Naphtali; and he also had Basemath, the daughter of Solomon, in marriage.
verses.4:16: Baana the son of Hushai, in Asher and in Bealoth.
verses.4:17: Shimei the son of Ela, in Benjamin.
verses.4:18: Geber the son of Uri, in the land of Gilead, in the land of Sihon king of the Amorites and of Og king of Bashan, over all things that were in that land.
verses.4:19: Jehoshaphat the son of Paruah, in Issachar.
verses.5:1: And the above-mentioned governors of the king provided food for them; moreover, they also supplied the necessities of the table of King Solomon with immense care in their due time. Barley also, and straw for the horses and beasts of burden, they brought to the place where the king was, according to what was appointed for them.
verses.5:2: Now the food of Solomon for each day was thirty cors of fine flour, and sixty cors of meal,
verses.5:3: ten fattened oxen, and twenty pasture-fed oxen, and a hundred rams, besides the game of stags, roe deer, and wild oxen, and fattened fowl.
verses.5:4: For he himself held the entire region that was beyond the river, from Tiphsah as far as Gaza, and all the kings of those regions; and he had peace on every side all around.
verses.5:9: God also gave wisdom to Solomon, and exceedingly great understanding, and breadth of heart like the sand that is on the shore of the sea.
verses.5:10: And the wisdom of Solomon surpassed the wisdom of all the people of the East and of the Egyptians,
verses.5:11: and he was wiser than all men: wiser than Ethan the Ezrahite, and Heman, and Calcol, and Darda, the sons of Mahol; and he was renowned among all the nations all around.
verses.5:12: Solomon also spoke three thousand parables, and his songs were one thousand and five.
verses.5:13: And he discoursed concerning trees, from the cedar that is in Lebanon to the hyssop that comes out of the wall; and he discussed beasts, and birds, and creeping things, and fish.
verses.5:14: Therefore the kingdom was established in the hand of Solomon, and he was joined in marriage alliance to Pharaoh, king of Egypt; for he took his daughter and brought her into the city of David, until he finished building his own house, and the house of the Lord, and the wall of Jerusalem all around. And they came from all the peoples to hear the wisdom of Solomon, and from all the kings of the earth who heard of his wisdom. Pharaoh, king of Egypt, went up and captured Gezer, and burned it with fire, and killed the Canaanite who lived in the city; and he gave it as a dowry to his daughter, the wife of Solomon.
verses.5:15: Hiram, king of Tyre, also sent his servants to Solomon; for he heard that they had anointed him king in place of his father, because Hiram had been a friend to David at all times.
verses.5:16: Now Solomon sent word to Hiram, saying:
verses.5:17: "You know the will of David my father, and that he could not build a house for the name of the Lord his God because of the wars threatening all around, until the Lord put them under the sole of his feet.
verses.5:18: But now the Lord my God has given me rest all around, and there is no adversary, nor evil encounter.
verses.5:19: For this reason I intend to build a temple for the name of the Lord my God, just as the Lord spoke to David my father, saying, 'Your son, whom I will set in your place upon your throne, he himself will build a house for My name.'
verses.5:20: Command therefore that your servants cut down cedars for me from Lebanon, and let my servants be with your servants; and I will give you the wages of your servants, whatever you ask; for you know how there is not a man among my people who knows how to cut timber like the Sidonians."
verses.5:21: Therefore, when Hiram heard the words of Solomon, he rejoiced greatly and said, "Blessed be the Lord God today, who has given David a most wise son over this very numerous people."
verses.5:22: And Hiram sent word to Solomon, saying, "I have heard whatever you have directed to me; I will carry out all your desire concerning cedar timber and fir timber.
verses.5:23: My servants will bring them down from Lebanon to the sea, and I will assemble them into rafts on the sea as far as the place that you indicate to me; and I will bring them ashore there, and you will take them; and you will supply the necessities for me, so that food may be given to my household."
verses.5:24: So Hiram kept giving Solomon cedar timber and fir timber, according to all his desire.
verses.5:25: And Solomon supplied Hiram twenty thousand cors of wheat as food for his household, and twenty cors of the purest oil; these things Solomon gave to Hiram each year.
verses.5:26: And the Lord gave wisdom to Solomon, just as He had spoken to him; and there was peace between Hiram and Solomon, and the two of them struck a covenant.
verses.5:27: And King Solomon selected laborers out of all Israel, and the levy was thirty thousand men.
verses.5:28: And he sent them to Lebanon, ten thousand each month in turns, so that for two months they were in their own homes; and Adoniram was over this kind of levy.
verses.5:29: And Solomon had seventy thousand of those who carried burdens, and eighty thousand stonecutters in the mountain,
verses.5:30: besides the overseers who were in charge of the individual works, three thousand three hundred in number, commanding the people and those who were doing the work.
verses.5:32: These the masons of Solomon and the masons of Hiram hewed; moreover, the Gebalites prepared timber and stones for building the house.
verses.6:1: And the king commanded that they take great stones, costly stones for the foundation of the temple, and square them. Therefore it came about in the four hundred and eightieth year from the departure of the sons of Israel out of the land of Egypt, in the fourth year of the reign of Solomon over Israel, in the month of Ziv (that is the second month), that the house began to be built for the Lord. In the fourth year the house of the Lord was founded in the month of Ziv; and in the eleventh year, in the month of Bul (that is the eighth month), the house was completed in all its work and in all its utensils; and he built it in seven years.
verses.6:2: Now the house that King Solomon was building for the Lord had sixty cubits in length, and twenty cubits in width, and thirty cubits in height.
verses.6:3: And there was a portico before the temple, twenty cubits in length, according to the measure of the width of the temple; and it had ten cubits in width before the face of the temple.
verses.6:4: And he made oblique windows in the temple.
verses.6:5: And he built stories against the wall of the temple in a circuit, on the walls of the house around the temple and the oracle, and he made side chambers all around.
verses.6:6: The story that was underneath had five cubits in width, and the middle story was six cubits in width, and the third story had seven cubits in width. Moreover, he placed beams on the house all around on the outside, so that they would not attach to the walls of the temple.
verses.6:7: Now the house, as it was being built, was built of hewn and finished stones; and no hammer, nor axe, nor any iron tool was heard in the house as it was being built.
verses.6:8: The door of the middle side chamber was on the right side of the house; and by a winding staircase they went up into the middle upper chamber, and from the middle into the third.
verses.6:9: And he built the house and finished it; he also covered the house with paneled ceilings of cedar.
verses.6:10: And he built a story over the entire house, five cubits in height, and he overlaid the house with cedar wood.
verses.6:15: And he built the walls of the house on the inside with cedar paneling; from the floor of the house up to the top of the walls, and up to the paneled ceilings, he overlaid them with cedar wood on the inside; and he covered the floor of the house with fir planks.
verses.6:16: And he built cedar paneling of twenty cubits at the rear part of the temple, from the floor up to the upper parts; and he made the inner house of the oracle as the Holy of Holies.
verses.6:17: Moreover, the temple itself before the doors of the oracle was forty cubits.
verses.6:19: Now he had made the oracle in the middle of the house, in the interior part, so that he might place there the ark of the covenant of the Lord.
verses.6:20: Furthermore, the oracle had twenty cubits in length, and twenty cubits in width, and twenty cubits in height; and he overlaid and clad it with the purest gold; and he also clad the altar with cedar.
verses.6:21: He also overlaid the house before the oracle with the purest gold, and fastened the plates with golden nails.
verses.6:22: And there was nothing in the temple that was not covered with gold; and he also covered the entire altar of the oracle with gold.
verses.6:23: And he made in the oracle two cherubim of olive wood, ten cubits in height.
verses.6:24: One wing of the cherub was five cubits, and the other wing of the cherub was five cubits; that is, having ten cubits from the tip of one wing to the tip of the other wing.
verses.6:25: The second cherub was also ten cubits; the two cherubim were of equal measure and one workmanship,
verses.6:26: that is, one cherub had a height of ten cubits, and likewise the second cherub.
verses.6:27: And he placed the cherubim in the middle of the inner temple; and the cherubim stretched out their wings, and one wing touched the wall, and the wing of the second cherub touched the other wall; while the other wings touched one another in the middle part of the temple.
verses.6:28: He also covered the cherubim with gold.
verses.6:29: And he carved all the walls of the temple all around with varied engravings and turned work; and he made on them cherubim, and palm trees, and various figures, as if projecting from the wall and coming out.
verses.6:30: And he also covered the floor of the house with gold inside and outside.
verses.6:31: And at the entrance of the oracle he made small doors of olive wood, and doorposts of five angles.
verses.6:32: And two doors of olive wood; and he carved on them the figure of cherubim, and likenesses of palm trees, and greatly projecting reliefs; and he covered them with gold, and overlaid both the cherubim and the palm trees, and the rest, with gold.
verses.6:33: And he made at the entrance of the temple four-angled doorposts of olive wood,
verses.6:34: and two doors of fir wood on either side; and each door was double, and opened while holding together.
verses.6:35: And he carved cherubim, and palm trees, and very prominent engravings; and he overlaid all of them with golden plates in squared work according to the rule.
verses.6:36: And he built the inner court with three courses of polished stones, and one course of cedar timbers.

verses.7:3: And he fashioned two bronze pillars, one pillar eighteen cubits in height, and a line of twelve cubits encircled each pillar.
verses.7:4: He also made two capitals to be placed on the tops of the pillars, cast from bronze: one capital five cubits in height, and the other capital five cubits in height,
verses.7:5: and as it were in the manner of a net, and of chains interwoven with one another in marvelous workmanship. Each capital of the pillars was cast: seven networks in rows on the one capital, and seven networks on the other capital.
verses.7:6: And he finished the pillars, and two rows of pomegranates around each network to cover the capitals that were on the top; in the same way he did also for the second capital.
verses.7:7: And he set up the two pillars in the portico of the temple; and when he had set up the right pillar, he called it by the name Jachin; likewise he erected the second pillar, and called its name Boaz.
verses.7:8: Now the capitals that were on the tops of the pillars were crafted like lily work in the portico, of four cubits. And on the tops of the pillars he placed work in the manner of a lily; and the work of the pillars was finished.
verses.7:9: And again there were other capitals on the top of the pillars above, according to the measure of the pillar, opposite the networks; and there were two hundred rows of pomegranates around the second capital.
verses.7:10: He also made a cast sea ten cubits from rim to rim, round in circumference; its height was five cubits, and a cord of thirty cubits encircled it all around.
verses.7:11: And carving beneath the rim went around it, encompassing the sea for ten cubits; two rows of fluted carvings were cast.
verses.7:12: Now the thickness of the basin was three inches, and its rim was like the rim of a cup and the petal of a flared lily; it held two thousand baths.
verses.7:13: And it stood on twelve oxen, of which three faced toward the north, and three toward the west, and three toward the south, and three toward the east; and the sea was upon them above, and all their hindquarters were hidden inward.
verses.7:14: And he made ten bronze bases, each base four cubits in length, and four cubits in width, and three cubits in height.
verses.7:15: And the workmanship of the bases themselves was openwork, and there were carvings between the joints.
verses.7:16: And between the little crowns and the braids were lions, oxen, and cherubim, and on the joints likewise above; and beneath the lions and oxen, as it were straps of bronze hanging down.
verses.7:17: And there were four wheels for each base, and bronze axles; and on the four sides, as it were small shoulders cast beneath the basin, facing one another.
verses.7:18: The four wheels also that were at the four corners of the base were joined to one another beneath the base; one wheel had a height of a cubit and a half.
verses.7:19: Now the wheels were such as are customarily made for a chariot; and their axles, spokes, rims, and hubs were all cast.
verses.7:20: For those four small shoulders also, at each corner of one base, were cast and joined from the base itself.
verses.7:21: Now at the top of the base there was a certain roundness of half a cubit, so crafted that a basin could be placed on top of it, having its own engravings and varied carvings out of itself.
verses.7:23: In this manner he made ten bases, of one casting, measure, and similar carving.
verses.7:24: He also made ten bronze basins: one basin held forty baths, and it was of four cubits; and he placed each basin upon each one, that is, the ten bases.
verses.7:25: And he set the ten bases, five on the right side of the temple and five on the left; and the sea he placed on the right side of the temple, facing east toward the south.
verses.7:26: So Hiram made cauldrons, platters, and water vessels, and finished all the work of King Solomon in the temple of the Lord.
verses.7:27: Two pillars, and two cords of the capitals upon the capitals of the pillars, and two networks to cover the two cords that were on the tops of the pillars.
verses.7:28: And four hundred pomegranates on the two networks: two rows of pomegranates on each network, to cover the cords of the capitals that were on the tops of the pillars.
verses.7:29: And ten bases, and ten basins upon the bases.
verses.7:30: And one sea, and twelve oxen beneath the sea.
verses.7:31: The mouth of the basin also was on the inside at the summit of the head; and what appeared on the outside was one cubit, completely round, and altogether it had one cubit and a half; and at the corners of the pillars there were varied engravings, and the middle spaces between the pillars were square, not round.
verses.7:32: And Solomon placed all the vessels; yet because of the exceedingly great multitude, there was no weight of the bronze.
verses.7:33: In the plain region of the Jordan the king cast them, in clay soil, between Succoth and Zarethan.
verses.7:34: And Solomon made all the vessels in the house of the Lord: the golden altar, and the golden table on which the loaves of presentation were to be placed;
verses.7:35: and the golden lampstands, five on the right and five on the left in front of the oracle, of pure gold; and as it were lily blossoms, and golden lamps above, and golden tongs,
verses.7:36: and water jars, and small forks, and bowls, and small mortars, and censers, of purest gold; and the hinges of the doors of the inner house of the Holy of Holies, and of the doors of the house of the temple, were of gold.
verses.7:37: And Solomon finished all the work that he was doing in the house of the Lord, and brought in the things that his father David had consecrated, silver, gold, and vessels, and stored them in the treasuries of the house of the Lord.
verses.7:38: Now Solomon built his own house in thirteen years, and brought it all the way to completion.
verses.7:39: He also built the house of the forest of Lebanon, one hundred cubits in length, fifty cubits in width, and thirty cubits in height, and four walkways between cedar pillars; for he had cut cedar timbers into pillars.
verses.7:40: And with cedar planks he covered the entire chamber, which was supported by forty-five pillars. Now one row had fifteen pillars
verses.7:42: and facing one another directly, with equal space between the pillars, and above the pillars squared timbers equal in all respects.
verses.7:43: And he made a portico of pillars fifty cubits in length and thirty cubits in width, and another portico in front of the greater portico, and pillars, and architraves upon the pillars.
verses.7:44: He also made the portico of the throne, in which the tribunal is, and covered it with cedar timbers from the floor up to the top.
verses.7:45: And the small house, in which one sat to judge, was in the middle of the portico, of similar workmanship. He also made a house for Pharaoh's daughter (whom Solomon had taken as wife) of such workmanship as this portico.
verses.7:46: All were of costly stones, which had been sawed to a certain standard and measure both inside and outside, from the foundation up to the top of the walls, and on the outside as far as the greater courtyard.
verses.7:47: Now the foundations were of costly stones, large stones, of ten or eight cubits.
verses.7:48: And above, costly stones of equal measure had been cut, and likewise of cedar.
verses.7:49: And the greater courtyard was round, of three rows of cut stones and one row of dressed cedar, and also in the inner courtyard of the house of the Lord, and in the portico of the house.
verses.8:1: Then all the elders of Israel were gathered together with the chiefs of the tribes, and the leaders of the families of the sons of Israel, to King Solomon in Jerusalem, to bring the ark of the covenant of the Lord from the city of David, that is, from Zion.
verses.8:2: And all Israel assembled to King Solomon in the month of Ethanim, on the festival day; that is the seventh month.
verses.8:3: And all the elders from Israel came, and the priests took up the ark,
verses.8:4: and carried the ark of the Lord, and the tabernacle of the covenant, and all the vessels of the sanctuary that were in the tabernacle; and the priests and the Levites were carrying them.
verses.8:5: Now King Solomon, and all the multitude of Israel that had assembled to him, were walking with him before the ark, and they were sacrificing sheep and oxen without reckoning or number.
verses.8:6: And the priests brought the ark of the covenant of the Lord into its place, into the oracle of the temple, into the Holy of Holies, beneath the wings of the cherubim.
verses.8:7: For indeed the cherubim spread out their wings over the place of the ark, and covered the ark and its poles from above.
verses.8:8: And although the poles projected and their ends were visible outside the sanctuary before the oracle, they were not visible any further on the outside; and they have been there to the present day.
verses.8:9: Now in the ark there was nothing else except the two stone tablets that Moses had placed in it at Horeb, when the Lord made a covenant with the sons of Israel, as they were coming out of the land of Egypt.
verses.8:10: Now it happened, when the priests had come out of the sanctuary, that a cloud filled the house of the Lord,
verses.8:11: and the priests were unable to stand and minister because of the cloud, for the glory of the Lord had filled the house of the Lord.
verses.8:14: And the king turned his face and blessed the whole assembly of Israel; for the whole assembly of Israel was standing.
verses.8:15: And Solomon said, "Blessed be the Lord God of Israel, who spoke with His mouth to my father David and fulfilled it with His hands, saying,
verses.8:16: 'From the day on which I brought My people Israel out of Egypt, I did not choose a city from all the tribes of Israel so that a house might be built and My name might be there; but I chose David to be over My people Israel.'
verses.8:17: And my father David desired to build a house for the name of the Lord God of Israel;
verses.8:18: and the Lord said to my father David, 'Because you thought in your heart to build a house for My name, you did well, considering this very thing in your mind.
verses.8:19: Nevertheless, you will not build a house for Me, but your son, who will come out from your loins, he himself will build a house for My name.'
verses.8:20: The Lord has confirmed His word that He spoke; and I stood in place of my father David and sat on the throne of Israel, just as the Lord spoke, and I built a house for the name of the Lord God of Israel.
verses.8:21: And I appointed there a place for the ark, in which is the covenant of the Lord that He made with our fathers when they came out of the land of Egypt."
verses.8:22: Now Solomon stood before the altar of the Lord in the sight of the assembly of Israel, and spread out his hands toward heaven,
verses.8:23: and said, "Lord God of Israel, there is no god like You in heaven above or on the earth below, You who keep covenant and mercy for Your servants who walk before You with all their heart;
verses.8:24: You who have kept for Your servant my father David what You spoke to him: You spoke with Your mouth, and with Your hands You have fulfilled it, as this day proves.
verses.8:25: Now therefore, Lord God of Israel, keep for Your servant my father David what You spoke to him, saying, 'A man will not be taken away from you before Me to sit on the throne of Israel, only if your sons keep their way, so that they walk before Me just as you walked in My sight.'
verses.8:26: And now, Lord God of Israel, let Your words be confirmed that You spoke to Your servant my father David.
verses.8:27: Is it then to be thought that God truly dwells on the earth? For if heaven and the heavens of heavens cannot contain You, how much less this house that I have built?
verses.8:28: Yet look upon the prayer of Your servant and upon his petitions, Lord my God; hear the hymn and the prayer that Your servant prays before You today,
verses.8:29: that Your eyes may be open over this house night and day, over the house of which You said, 'My name will be there,' so that You may hear the prayer that Your servant prays to You in this place;
verses.8:30: that You may hear the supplication of Your servant and of Your people Israel, whatever they pray in this place; and You will hear in the place of Your dwelling in heaven, and when You hear, You will be merciful.
verses.8:31: If a man sins against his neighbor, and has some oath by which he is held bound, and comes because of the oath before Your altar into Your house,
verses.8:32: You will hear in heaven, and act, and judge Your servants, condemning the wicked man and returning his way upon his head, and justifying the righteous man and rewarding him according to his righteousness.
verses.8:33: If Your people Israel flee from their enemies (because they will sin against You), and, doing penance and confessing Your name, come and pray and make supplication to You in this house,
verses.8:34: hear in heaven, and forgive the sin of Your people Israel, and You will bring them back into the land that You gave to their fathers.
verses.8:35: If heaven is shut up, and it does not rain because of their sins, and praying in this place they do penance to Your name, and turn back from their sins because of their affliction,
verses.8:36: hear them in heaven, and forgive the sins of Your servants and of Your people Israel; and show them the good way along which they should walk, and give rain upon Your land, which You gave to Your people as a possession.
verses.8:37: If famine arises in the land, or pestilence, or corrupted air, or mildew, or locust, or rust, and their enemy afflicts them, besieging the gates; every plague, every sickness,
verses.8:38: every curse and imprecation that happens to any man of Your people Israel: if anyone knows the plague of his own heart, and spreads out his hands in this house,
verses.8:39: You will hear in heaven, in the place of Your dwelling, and be merciful, and act so that You give to each one according to all his ways, just as You see his heart (for You alone know the heart of all the sons of men),
verses.8:40: so that they may fear You all the days that they live upon the face of the land that You gave to our fathers.
verses.8:41: Moreover also the foreigner, who is not of Your people Israel, when he comes from a distant land because of Your name (for Your great name will be heard of, and Your strong hand, and Your arm
verses.8:42: stretched out everywhere), when he comes therefore and prays in this place,
verses.8:43: You will hear in heaven, in the foundation of Your dwelling, and do everything for which the foreigner calls upon You, so that all the peoples of the lands may learn to fear Your name, just as Your people Israel does, and may verify that Your name has been invoked over this house that I have built.
verses.8:44: If Your people go out to war against their enemies by the way, wherever You send them, they will pray to You toward the way of the city that You have chosen, and toward the house that I have built for Your name,
verses.8:45: and You will hear in heaven their prayers and their petitions, and execute their judgment.
verses.8:46: Now if they sin against You (for there is no man who does not sin), and being angry You hand them over to their enemies, and they are led captive into the land of the enemies, far or near,
verses.8:47: and they do penance in their heart in the place of captivity, and turning back they make supplication to You in their captivity, saying, 'We have sinned; we have acted iniquitously, we have done wickedly,'
verses.8:48: and they return to You with all their heart and all their soul in the land of their enemies to which they were led captive, and pray to You toward the way of their land, which You gave to their fathers, and of the city that You have chosen, and of the temple that I have built for Your name,
verses.8:49: You will hear in heaven, in the foundation of Your throne, their prayers and their petitions, and execute their judgment;
verses.8:50: and You will pardon Your people who have sinned against You, and all their iniquities by which they have transgressed against You; and You will grant mercy before those who hold them captive, so that they may have mercy on them.
verses.8:51: For they are Your people and Your inheritance, whom You brought out of the land of Egypt, from the midst of the iron furnace.
verses.8:52: May Your eyes be open to the supplication of Your servant and of Your people Israel, and may You hear them in all things for which they call upon You."
verses.8:53: Then Solomon said, "The Lord said that He would dwell in a cloud. Building, I have built a house for Your dwelling, Your most firm throne forever. For You separated them for Yourself as an inheritance from all the peoples of the earth, just as You spoke through Your servant Moses when You brought our fathers out of Egypt, Lord God."
verses.8:54: Now it happened, when Solomon had finished praying all this prayer and supplication to the Lord, that he rose from before the altar of the Lord; for he had fixed both knees on the ground and had spread out his hands toward heaven.
verses.8:55: Therefore he stood and blessed the whole assembly of Israel with a loud voice, saying,
verses.8:56: "Blessed be the Lord, who has given rest to His people Israel according to all that He spoke; not even one word has fallen from all the good things that He spoke through His servant Moses.
verses.8:57: May the Lord our God be with us, just as He was with our fathers, not abandoning nor casting us away.
verses.8:58: But may He incline our hearts to Himself, so that we may walk in all His ways and keep His commandments, and His ceremonies, and whatever judgments He commanded our fathers.
verses.8:59: And may these words of mine, with which I have made supplication before the Lord, be drawing near to the Lord our God day and night, so that He may execute judgment for His servant and for His people Israel day by day,
verses.8:60: so that all the peoples of the earth may know that the Lord Himself is God, and there is no other besides Him.
verses.8:61: May our heart also be perfect with the Lord our God, so that we may walk in His decrees and keep His commandments, just as also today."
verses.8:62: Therefore the king, and all Israel with him, were sacrificing victims before the Lord.
verses.8:63: And Solomon slaughtered peace offerings, which he sacrificed to the Lord: twenty-two thousand oxen and one hundred twenty thousand sheep; and the king and the sons of Israel dedicated the temple of the Lord.
verses.8:64: On that day the king sanctified the middle of the courtyard that was before the house of the Lord; for indeed he offered the burnt offering there, and the sacrifice, and the fat of the peace offerings, because the bronze altar that was before the Lord was too small and could not contain the burnt offering, and the sacrifice, and the fat of the peace offerings.
verses.8:65: Therefore Solomon held a celebrated festival at that time, and all Israel with him, a great multitude from the entrance of Hamath as far as the brook of Egypt, before the Lord our God, for seven days and seven days, that is, fourteen days.
verses.8:66: And on the eighth day he dismissed the peoples; and blessing the king, they departed to their tents rejoicing and with a cheerful heart over all the good things that the Lord had done for His servant David and for His people Israel.
verses.9:1: Now it happened, when Solomon had completed the building of the house of the Lord, and the building of the king, and everything that he had desired and wanted to do,
verses.9:2: that the Lord appeared to him a second time, just as He had appeared to him in Gibeon.
verses.9:3: And the Lord said to him, "I have heard your prayer and your plea, which you pleaded before Me; I have sanctified this house that you built, so that I might place My name there forever, and My eyes and My heart will be there for all days.
verses.9:4: You also, if you walk before Me just as your father walked, in simplicity of heart and in uprightness, and do everything that I have commanded you, and observe My statutes and My judgments,
verses.9:5: I will set the throne of your kingdom over Israel forever, just as I spoke to David your father, saying, 'A man of your lineage will not be removed from the throne of Israel.'
verses.9:6: But if you completely turn away, you and your sons, not following Me, nor keeping My commandments and My ceremonies that I have set before you, but go away and serve foreign gods and worship them,
verses.9:7: then I will remove Israel from the surface of the land that I gave them, and the temple that I sanctified for My name I will cast away from My sight; and Israel will become a proverb and a tale to all peoples.
verses.9:8: And this house will become an example; everyone who passes by it will be astonished and will hiss, and will say, 'Why has the Lord done so to this land and to this house?'
verses.9:9: And they will answer, 'Because they abandoned the Lord their God, who brought their fathers out of the land of Egypt, and followed foreign gods, and worshiped them, and served them; therefore the Lord has brought all this evil upon them.'" Now Pharaoh's daughter went up from the city of David into her own house, which Solomon had built for her; then he built Millo.
verses.9:10: Now when twenty years had been completed after Solomon had built the two houses, that is, the house of the Lord and the house of the king
verses.9:11: (with Hiram, king of Tyre, supplying Solomon with cedar and fir wood, and gold according to all that he had needed), then Solomon gave Hiram twenty towns in the land of Galilee.
verses.9:12: And Hiram went out from Tyre to see the towns that Solomon had given him, and they did not please him.
verses.9:13: And he said, "Are these the cities that you have given me, brother?" And he called them the land of Cabul, up to this day.
verses.9:14: Hiram also sent to King Solomon one hundred twenty talents of gold.
verses.9:26: King Solomon also built a fleet at Ezion-geber, which is near Elath on the shore of the Red Sea, in the land of Edom.
verses.9:27: And Hiram sent in that fleet his servants, men who were sailors and knowledgeable about the sea, with the servants of Solomon.
verses.9:28: And when they had come to Ophir, they took from there four hundred twenty talents of gold and brought it to King Solomon.
verses.10:1: Now the queen of Sheba also, having heard of Solomon's fame in the name of the Lord, came to test him with riddles.
verses.10:2: And having entered Jerusalem with a large retinue and riches, with camels carrying spices, and an exceedingly vast amount of gold, and precious gems, she came to King Solomon and spoke to him of everything that she had in her heart.
verses.10:3: And Solomon explained to her all the matters that she had put forward; there was not a word that could be hidden from the king so that he did not answer her.
verses.10:4: Now when the queen of Sheba saw all the wisdom of Solomon, and the house that he had built,
verses.10:5: and the foods of his table, and the dwellings of his servants, and the ranks of the attendants, and their garments, and the cupbearers, and the burnt offerings that he offered in the house of the Lord, she had no spirit left.
verses.10:6: And she said to the king, "The report is true that I heard in my land
verses.10:7: concerning your words and concerning your wisdom; and I did not believe those who told me, until I myself came and saw with my own eyes, and confirmed that half had not been reported to me; your wisdom and works are greater than the rumor that I heard.
verses.10:8: Happy are your men, and happy are your servants, who stand before you always and hear your wisdom.
verses.10:9: May the Lord your God be blessed, who was pleased with you and set you upon the throne of Israel, because the Lord has loved Israel forever, and appointed you king to administer judgment and justice."
verses.10:10: So she gave the king one hundred twenty talents of gold, and exceedingly abundant spices, and precious gems; never again were so many spices brought as those that the queen of Sheba gave to King Solomon.
verses.10:11: (Moreover, Hiram's fleet, which carried gold from Ophir, brought from Ophir exceedingly abundant thyine wood and precious gems.
verses.10:12: And from the thyine wood the king made supports for the house of the Lord and for the royal house, as well as harps and lyres for the singers; no thyine wood of this kind has been brought, nor seen, up to the present day.)
verses.10:13: Now King Solomon gave the queen of Sheba everything that she wanted and asked of him, apart from those things that he had freely offered her as a royal gift. Then she returned and departed to her own land with her servants.
verses.10:14: Now the weight of gold that was brought to Solomon every year was six hundred sixty-six talents of gold,
verses.10:15: apart from what was brought by the men who were over the revenues, and the merchants, and all those selling small wares, and all the kings of Arabia, and the governors of the land.
verses.10:16: King Solomon also made two hundred large shields of purest gold; he put six hundred shekels of gold into the plates of one shield.
verses.10:17: And three hundred small shields of tested gold; three hundred minas of gold overlaid one small shield; and the king placed them in the house of the forest of Lebanon.
verses.10:18: King Solomon also made a great throne of ivory, and overlaid it with gold of an exceedingly deep yellow,
verses.10:19: which had six steps; and the top of the throne was round at the back; and there were two arms on this side and that holding the seat; and two lions stood beside each arm.
verses.10:20: And twelve small lions were standing upon the six steps, on this side and that; such a work has not been made in all the kingdoms.
verses.10:21: Moreover, all the vessels from which King Solomon drank were of gold, and all the furnishings of the house of the forest of Lebanon were of purest gold; there was no silver, nor was it considered of any value in the days of Solomon.
verses.10:22: This is the sum of the expenses that King Solomon provided for building the house of the Lord and his own house, and Millo, and the wall of Jerusalem, and Hazor, and Megiddo, and Gezer. So Solomon built Gezer, and lower Beth-horon, and Baalath, and Palmyra in the land of the wilderness. And he fortified all the villages that belonged to him and were without a wall, and the cities of chariots and the cities of horsemen, and whatever pleased him to build in Jerusalem, and in Lebanon, and in all the land of his dominion. All the people who had remained from the Amorites, and the Hittites, and the Perizzites, and the Hivites, and the Jebusites, who are not of the sons of Israel: their sons who had remained in the land, namely those whom the sons of Israel had not been able to wipe out, Solomon made subject to tribute up to this day. But of the sons of Israel Solomon did not appoint anyone to serve; rather, they were fighting men, and his ministers, and princes, and commanders, and officers of chariots and horses. For the king's fleet went by sea with Hiram's fleet once every three years to Tarshish, bringing from there gold, and silver, and elephant tusks, and apes, and peacocks.
verses.10:23: So King Solomon was magnified above all the kings of the earth in riches and wisdom.
verses.10:24: And all the earth longed for the presence of Solomon, to hear his wisdom, which God had given in his heart.
verses.10:25: And each one brought him gifts: vessels of silver and gold, garments and weapons of war, spices also, and horses and mules, every year.
verses.10:26: And Solomon had forty thousand stalls for chariot horses and twelve thousand riding horses. And Solomon gathered chariots and horsemen, and he had one thousand four hundred chariots and twelve thousand horsemen; and he stationed them throughout the fortified cities, and with the king in Jerusalem.
verses.10:27: And he caused there to be as great an abundance of silver in Jerusalem as of stones; and he supplied a multitude of cedars like the sycamores that grow in the plains.
verses.10:28: And horses were brought out for Solomon from Egypt and from Kue. For the king's merchants bought them from Kue and brought them at a fixed price.
verses.10:29: Now a chariot came out from Egypt for six hundred shekels of silver, and a horse for one hundred fifty. And in this way all the kings of the Hittites and of Syria sold horses.
verses.11:1: Now King Solomon deeply loved many foreign women, the daughter of Pharaoh as well, and Moabite, Ammonite, Edomite, Sidonian, and Hittite women. And he had seven hundred wives as queens and three hundred concubines, and the women turned his heart away.
verses.11:2: From the nations concerning which the Lord said to the sons of Israel, "You shall not go in to them, nor shall any of them go in to your women, for most certainly they will turn your hearts away so that you follow their gods"—to these, therefore, Solomon was joined with the most ardent love.
verses.11:4: And when he was already old, his heart was corrupted by the women, so that he followed foreign gods; nor was his heart perfect with the Lord his God, like the heart of David his father.
verses.11:5: Then Solomon built a shrine for Chemosh, the idol of Moab, on the mountain that is opposite Jerusalem, and for Molech, the idol of the sons of Ammon.
verses.11:6: But Solomon worshiped Ashtoreth, the goddess of the Sidonians, and Molech, the idol of the Ammonites.
verses.11:7: And in this way he did for all his foreign wives, who burned incense and offered sacrifices to their gods.
verses.11:8: And Solomon did what had not been pleasing before the Lord, and he did not fully follow the Lord like David his father.
verses.11:9: Therefore the Lord was angry with Solomon, because his mind had been turned away from the Lord God of Israel, who had appeared to him a second time,
verses.11:10: and had commanded concerning this matter that he should not follow foreign gods; yet he did not keep what the Lord commanded him.
verses.11:11: Therefore the Lord said to Solomon, "Because you have had this with you, and have not kept My covenant and My precepts that I commanded you, breaking it apart, I will tear your kingdom and give it to your servant.
verses.11:12: Nevertheless, in your days I will not do it, for the sake of David your father; from the hand of your son I will tear it,
verses.11:13: nor will I take away the whole kingdom, but I will give one tribe to your son for the sake of David My servant, and for Jerusalem, which I have chosen."
verses.11:14: Now the Lord raised up an adversary against Solomon, Hadad the Edomite, of the royal seed, who was in Edom. God also raised up against him an adversary, Rezon the son of Eliada, who had fled from Hadadezer king of Zobah, his master; and he gathered men against him, and became a leader of bandits when David was killing them. And they went away to Damascus and lived there, and they appointed him king in Damascus.
verses.11:15: For when David was in Edom, and Joab the commander of the army had gone up to bury those who had been killed, and had put to death every male in Edom
verses.11:16: (for Joab and all Israel remained there six months, until he had wiped out every male in Edom),
verses.11:17: Hadad himself fled, and Edomite men from the servants of his father with him, to enter Egypt; now Hadad was a little boy.
verses.11:18: And when they had risen from Midian, they came to Paran; and they took men from Paran with them and entered Egypt, to Pharaoh king of Egypt, who gave him a house, appointed food, and assigned land.
verses.11:19: And Hadad found great favor before Pharaoh, to such an extent that he gave him as a wife the full sister of his own wife, Queen Tahpenes.
verses.11:20: And the sister of Tahpenes bore him a son, Genubath, and Tahpenes raised him in the house of Pharaoh; and Genubath was living with Pharaoh among his sons.
verses.11:21: And when Hadad had heard in Egypt that David had slept with his fathers, and that Joab the commander of the army was dead, he said to Pharaoh, "Send me away, so that I may go to my land."
verses.11:22: And Pharaoh said to him, "What then do you lack with me, that you seek to go to your land?" And he answered, "Nothing; yet I beg you to send me away."
verses.11:25: And he was an adversary to Israel all the days of Solomon; and this is the evil of Hadad, and the hatred against Israel; and he reigned in Syria.
verses.11:26: Jeroboam also, the son of Nebat, an Ephrathite from Zeredah, a servant of Solomon, whose mother was named Zeruah, a widowed woman, raised his hand against the king.
verses.11:27: And this is the cause of the rebellion against him: that Solomon built the Millo and leveled the chasm of the city of David his father.
verses.11:28: Now Jeroboam was a strong and mighty man; and Solomon, seeing that the young man was of good character and industrious, had appointed him overseer over the tributes of the entire house of Joseph.
verses.11:29: Therefore it happened at that time that Jeroboam went out from Jerusalem, and Ahijah the Shilonite, the prophet, found him on the road, wrapped in a new cloak; now the two of them alone were in the field.
verses.11:30: And taking hold of his new cloak in which he was wrapped, Ahijah tore it into twelve pieces.
verses.11:31: And he said to Jeroboam, "Take for yourself ten torn pieces, for this is what the Lord God of Israel says: 'Look, I will tear the kingdom from the hand of Solomon, and I will give you ten tribes.
verses.11:32: However, one tribe will remain to him for the sake of My servant David, and for Jerusalem, the city that I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel,
verses.11:33: because he has abandoned Me, and has worshiped Ashtoreth, the goddess of the Sidonians, and Chemosh, the god of Moab, and Molech, the god of the sons of Ammon; and he has not walked in My ways to do righteousness before Me, and My precepts and judgments, like David his father.
verses.11:34: Nor will I take away the whole kingdom from his hand, but I will set him as ruler all the days of his life, for the sake of David My servant whom I chose, who kept My commandments and My precepts.
verses.11:35: But I will take away the kingdom from the hand of his son, and I will give you ten tribes;
verses.11:36: yet to his son I will give one tribe, so that a lamp may remain for David My servant through all days before Me in Jerusalem, the city that I have chosen so that My name might be there.
verses.11:37: You, however, I will take, and you will reign over everything that your soul desires, and you will be king over Israel.
verses.11:38: If, therefore, you listen to all that I command you, and walk in My ways, and do what is right before Me, keeping My commandments and My precepts, just as David My servant did, I will be with you, and I will build for you a faithful house, just as I built a house for David, and I will deliver Israel to you.'"
verses.11:40: Solomon therefore wanted to kill Jeroboam; and he rose and fled into Egypt to Shishak king of Egypt, and was in Egypt until the death of Solomon.
verses.11:41: Now the rest of the words of Solomon, and all that he did, and his wisdom—see, all of them are written in the book of the words of the days of Solomon.
verses.11:42: And the days that Solomon reigned in Jerusalem over all Israel are forty years.
verses.11:43: And Solomon slept with his fathers, and was buried in the city of David his father; and Rehoboam his son reigned in his place. Meanwhile, Jeroboam the son of Nebat, while he was still in Egypt as a fugitive from the face of King Solomon, upon hearing of his death, returned from Egypt.
verses.12:1: Now Rehoboam came to Shechem, for all Israel had gathered there to appoint him king.
verses.12:3: And they sent and called him; therefore Jeroboam and the entire multitude of Israel came and spoke to Rehoboam, saying,
verses.12:4: "Your father placed a most harsh yoke upon us; now therefore, lessen a little of the most harsh rule of your father, and of the heaviest yoke that he placed upon us, and we will serve you."
verses.12:5: And he said to them, "Go until the third day, and return to me." And when the people had departed,
verses.12:6: King Rehoboam took counsel with the elders who stood before Solomon his father while he was still alive, and he said, "What counsel do you give me, so that I may answer this people?"
verses.12:7: And they said to him, "If today you obey this people, and serve them, and yield to their petition, and speak gentle words to them, they will be servants to you through all days."
verses.12:8: But he abandoned the counsel of the old men that they had given him, and consulted the young men who had been raised with him and stood before him,
verses.12:9: and he said to them, "What counsel do you give me, so that I may answer this people, who have said to me, 'Make lighter the yoke that your father placed upon us'?"
verses.12:10: And the young men who had been raised with him said to him, "In this way you shall speak to this people, who have spoken to you, saying, 'Your father made our yoke heavy; you relieve us.' In this way you shall speak to them: 'My little finger is thicker than the back of my father.
verses.12:11: And now my father laid a heavy yoke upon you, but I will add to your yoke; my father beat you with whips, but I will beat you with scorpions.'"
verses.12:12: Therefore Jeroboam and all the people came to Rehoboam on the third day, just as the king had spoken, saying, "Return to me on the third day."
verses.12:13: And the king answered the people harshly, having abandoned the counsel of the elders that they had given him,
verses.12:14: and he spoke to them according to the counsel of the young men, saying, "My father made your yoke heavy, but I will add to your yoke; my father beat you with whips, but I will beat you with scorpions."
verses.12:15: And the king did not yield to the people, because the Lord had turned away from him, so that He might establish His word which He had spoken by the hand of Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam the son of Nebat.
verses.12:16: Therefore the people, seeing that the king had been unwilling to listen to them, answered him, saying, "What share do we have in David? Or what inheritance in the son of Jesse? Go to your tents, Israel! Now see to your own house, David!" And Israel went away to their tents.
verses.12:18: King Rehoboam therefore sent Adoram, who was over the tributes, and all Israel stoned him, and he died. Meanwhile, King Rehoboam hastily mounted a chariot and fled to Jerusalem;
verses.12:19: and Israel withdrew from the house of David to the present day.
verses.12:20: Now it happened when all Israel had heard that Jeroboam had returned, that they sent and called him after gathering the assembly, and appointed him king over all Israel; and no one followed the house of David except the tribe of Judah alone.
verses.12:21: Now Rehoboam came to Jerusalem and gathered the entire house of Judah and the tribe of Benjamin, one hundred and eighty thousand chosen fighting men, to fight against the house of Israel and restore the kingdom to Rehoboam the son of Solomon.
verses.12:22: But the word of the Lord came to Shemaiah, the man of God, saying,
verses.12:23: "Speak to Rehoboam the son of Solomon, king of Judah, and to all the house of Judah and Benjamin, and the rest of the people, saying,
verses.12:24: 'This is what the Lord says: You shall not go up, nor shall you wage war against your brothers, the sons of Israel; let each man return to his house, for from Me this thing has come about.'" They listened to the word of the Lord and turned back from the journey, just as the Lord had commanded them. At that time Abijah the son of Jeroboam fell ill. And Jeroboam said to his wife, "Rise and change your attire, so that you are not recognized as being the wife of Jeroboam, and go to Shiloh, where Ahijah the prophet is, who spoke to me that I would reign over this people. Take also in your hand ten loaves, and a cake, and a jar of honey, and go to him; for he himself will tell you what is going to happen to this boy." The wife of Jeroboam did as he had said; and rising up, she went away to Shiloh and came to the house of Ahijah; but he could not see, because his eyes had grown dim from old age. Now the Lord said to Ahijah, "Look, the wife of Jeroboam is coming in to consult you concerning her son, who is sick; you shall speak this and that to her." Therefore when she was entering and concealing who she was, Ahijah heard the sound of her feet entering through the doorway, and he said, "Come in, wife of Jeroboam! Why do you pretend to be another woman? Yet I have been sent to you as a harsh messenger. Therefore, look, I will bring evils upon the house of Jeroboam, and I will strike down from Jeroboam the one who urinates against a wall, both the confined and the last in Israel; and I will clean out the remnants of the house of Jeroboam, just as dung is usually cleaned out until it is clean. Those of Jeroboam who die in the city, dogs will eat; and those who die in the field, the birds of the sky will devour; for the Lord has spoken. You, therefore, rise and go to your house; and at the very entrance of your feet into the city, the boy will die, and all Israel will mourn him and bury him; for this one alone from Jeroboam will be carried into a tomb, because a good word from the Lord God of Israel has been found concerning him in the house of Jeroboam." Therefore the wife of Jeroboam rose, went away, and came to Tirzah; and as she was entering the threshold of the house, the boy died, and they buried him. And all Israel mourned him according to the word of the Lord, which He spoke by the hand of His servant Ahijah the prophet.
verses.12:25: Now Jeroboam built Shechem on Mount Ephraim and lived there; and going out from there, he built Penuel.
verses.12:26: And Jeroboam said in his heart, "Now the kingdom will return to the house of David,
verses.12:27: if this people goes up to offer sacrifices in the house of the Lord in Jerusalem; then the heart of this people will turn back to their lord, Rehoboam king of Judah, and they will kill me and return to him."
verses.12:28: And having devised a plan, he made two golden calves and said to them, "Do not go up to Jerusalem any longer; here are your gods, Israel, who brought you out of the land of Egypt!"
verses.12:29: And he placed one in Bethel, and the other in Dan;
verses.12:30: and this thing became a sin, for the people went to worship the calf as far as Dan.
verses.12:31: And he made shrines on the high places, and priests from the lowest of the people, who were not from the sons of Levi.
verses.12:32: And he appointed a solemn feast day in the eighth month, on the fifteenth day of the month, in the likeness of the solemn feast that was celebrated in Judah. And going up to the altar, he did likewise in Bethel, to offer sacrifices to the calves that he had fashioned; and he appointed in Bethel priests of the high places that he had made.
verses.12:33: And he went up onto the altar that he had constructed in Bethel, on the fifteenth day of the eighth month, which he had invented out of his own heart; and he made a solemn feast for the sons of Israel, and went up onto the altar to burn incense.
verses.13:1: And look, a man of God came from Judah by the word of the Lord to Bethel, while Jeroboam was standing over the altar and casting incense.
verses.13:2: And he cried out against the altar by the word of the Lord and said, "Altar, altar, this is what the Lord says: 'Look, a son will be born to the house of David, Josiah by name, and he will sacrifice upon you the priests of the high places who now kindle incense on you, and he will burn human bones upon you.'"
verses.13:3: And on that day he gave a sign, saying, "This will be the sign that the Lord has spoken: look, the altar will be split apart, and the ashes that are on it will be poured out."
verses.13:4: And when the king heard the word of the man of God that he had cried out against the altar in Bethel, he stretched out his hand from the altar, saying, "Seize him." And his hand, which he had stretched out against him, withered, and he was not able to pull it back to himself.
verses.13:5: The altar also was split apart, and the ashes were poured out from the altar, according to the sign that the man of God had foretold by the word of the Lord.
verses.13:6: And the king said to the man of God, "Implore the face of the Lord your God, and pray for me, so that my hand may be restored to me." And the man of God prayed to the face of the Lord, and the king's hand returned to him and became as it had been before.
verses.13:7: Now the king spoke to the man of God, "Come home with me to dine, and I will give you gifts."
verses.13:8: And the man of God answered the king, "If you give me half of your house, I will not come with you, nor will I eat bread or drink water in this place;
