verses.13:9: for thus it was commanded to me by the word of the Lord, who ordered, 'You must not eat bread, nor drink water, nor return by the way by which you came.'"
verses.13:10: So he went away by another way, and did not return by the road by which he had come to Bethel.
verses.13:11: Now a certain old prophet lived in Bethel, to whom his sons came, and they recounted to him all the deeds that the man of God had done that day in Bethel; and the words that he had spoken to the king they recounted to their father.
verses.13:12: And their father said to them, "By which way did he go?" His sons showed him the way by which the man of God who had come from Judah had gone.
verses.13:13: And he said to his sons, "Saddle the donkey for me." When they had saddled it, he mounted,
verses.13:14: and went after the man of God, and found him sitting under a terebinth tree; and he said to him, "Are you the man of God who came from Judah?" He answered, "I am."
verses.13:15: And he said to him, "Come home with me to eat bread."
verses.13:16: He said, "I cannot return, nor come with you, nor will I eat bread or drink water in this place,
verses.13:17: for the Lord spoke to me by the word of the Lord, saying, 'You must not eat bread and you must not drink water there, nor return by the way by which you went.'"
verses.13:18: He said to him, "I too am a prophet like you, and an angel spoke to me by the word of the Lord, saying, 'Bring him back with you into your house, so that he may eat bread and drink water.'" He deceived him,
verses.13:19: and brought him back with him; so he ate bread in his house and drank water.
verses.13:20: And while they were sitting at the table, the word of the Lord came to the prophet who had brought him back.
verses.13:21: And he cried out to the man of God who had come from Judah, saying, "This is what the Lord says: 'Because you were not obedient to the mouth of the Lord and did not keep the command that the Lord your God commanded you,
verses.13:22: and returned and ate bread and drank water in the place in which He commanded you not to eat bread or drink water, your corpse will not be brought into the tomb of your fathers.'"
verses.13:23: And when he had eaten and drunk, he saddled his donkey for the prophet whom he had brought back.
verses.13:24: When he had departed, a lion found him on the road and killed him, and his corpse was thrown on the path; now the donkey was standing beside him, and the lion was standing beside the corpse.
verses.13:25: And look, men passing by saw the corpse thrown on the road and the lion standing beside the corpse. And they came and spread the news in the city in which that old prophet lived.
verses.13:26: When that prophet who had brought him back from the road heard this, he said, "It is the man of God who was disobedient to the mouth of the Lord, and the Lord handed him over to the lion, and it crushed him and killed him, according to the word of the Lord that He spoke to him."
verses.13:28: and he had departed, he found his corpse thrown on the road, and the donkey and the lion standing beside the corpse; the lion had not eaten from the corpse, nor had it harmed the donkey.
verses.13:29: So the prophet lifted up the corpse of the man of God and placed it upon the donkey, and returning, he brought it into the city of the old prophet to mourn him.
verses.13:30: And he laid his corpse in his own tomb, and they mourned him: "Oh, oh, my brother!"
verses.13:31: And when they had mourned him, he said to his sons, "When I die, bury me in the tomb in which the man of God is buried; lay my bones beside his bones.
verses.13:32: For surely the word that he foretold by the word of the Lord will come about against the altar that is in Bethel, and against all the shrines of the high places that are in the cities of Samaria."
verses.13:33: After these words Jeroboam did not turn back from his most wicked way, but on the contrary he made priests of the high places from the lowest of the people; whoever wished filled his hand and became a priest of the high places.
verses.13:34: And for this reason the house of Jeroboam sinned, and was overthrown and wiped out from the surface of the earth.
verses.14:21: Now Rehoboam the son of Solomon reigned in Judah. Rehoboam was forty-one years old when he began to reign; he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city that the Lord chose out of all the tribes of Israel to place His name there. And his mother's name was Naamah the Ammonite.
verses.14:22: And Judah did evil before the Lord, and they provoked Him above all that their fathers had done, in their sins that they committed.
verses.14:23: For they also built for themselves altars, and statues, and groves upon every high hill and under every leafy tree.
verses.14:24: Moreover, there were also effeminate men in the land, and they did all the abominations of the nations that the Lord crushed before the face of the sons of Israel.
verses.14:25: Now in the fifth year of the reign of Rehoboam, Shishak king of Egypt went up against Jerusalem,
verses.14:26: and took the treasures of the house of the Lord and the royal treasures, and plundered everything, as well as the golden shields that Solomon had made;
verses.14:27: in place of which King Rehoboam made bronze shields, and delivered them into the hand of the commanders of the shield-bearers and of those who kept watch before the door of the king's house.
verses.14:28: And whenever the king entered the house of the Lord, those who had the duty of going ahead carried them, and afterward they brought them back to the armory of the shield-bearers.
verses.14:29: Now the rest of the words of Rehoboam, and all that he did, look, they are written in the book of the words of the days of the kings of Judah.
verses.14:30: And there was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam all the days.
verses.14:31: And Rehoboam slept with his fathers and was buried with them in the city of David; and his mother's name was Naamah the Ammonite; and Abijam his son reigned in his place.
verses.15:1: So in the eighteenth year of the reign of Jeroboam son of Nebat, Abijam reigned over Judah.
verses.15:2: For three years he reigned in Jerusalem; the name of his mother was Maacah, daughter of Absalom.
verses.15:3: And he walked in all the sins of his father, which he had done before him; and his heart was not perfect with the Lord his God, like the heart of David his father.
verses.15:4: But for David's sake the Lord his God gave him a lamp in Jerusalem, so that He might raise up his son after him and establish Jerusalem,
verses.15:5: because David had done what was right in the eyes of the Lord, and had not turned aside from all that He had commanded him all the days of his life, except in the matter of Uriah the Hittite.
verses.15:7: Now the rest of the matters of Abijam, and all that he did, are these not written in the book of the words of the days of the kings of Judah? And there was battle between Abijam and Jeroboam.
verses.15:8: And Abijam slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the city of David; and Asa his son reigned in his place.
verses.15:9: Therefore in the twentieth year of Jeroboam king of Israel, Asa reigned as king of Judah,
verses.15:10: and for forty-one years he reigned in Jerusalem. The name of his mother was Maacah, daughter of Absalom.
verses.15:11: And Asa did what was right before the sight of the Lord, like David his father;
verses.15:12: and he removed the effeminate men from the land, and purged all the filth of the idols that his fathers had made.
verses.15:13: Moreover, he also removed Maacah his mother, so that she would not be leader in the sacred rites of Priapus and in his grove that she had consecrated; and he overthrew his cavern, and shattered the most shameful image, and burned it in the brook Kidron;
verses.15:14: yet he did not remove the high places. Nevertheless, the heart of Asa was perfect with the Lord all his days;
verses.15:15: and he brought the things that his father had sanctified and vowed into the house of the Lord: silver, and gold, and vessels.
verses.15:16: Now there was war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel all their days.
verses.15:17: Baasha king of Israel also went up against Judah and built Ramah, so that no one could go out or come in from the side of Asa king of Judah.
verses.15:18: Therefore Asa took all the silver and gold that had remained in the treasuries of the house of the Lord and in the treasuries of the royal house, and gave it into the hands of his servants; and he sent to Ben-hadad son of Tabrimmon, son of Hezion, king of Syria, who lived in Damascus, saying,
verses.15:19: "There is a treaty between me and you, and between my father and your father; therefore I have sent you gifts, silver and gold, and I ask that you come and make void the treaty that you have with Baasha king of Israel, so that he may withdraw from me."
verses.15:20: Consenting to King Asa, Ben-hadad sent the commanders of his army against the cities of Israel, and they struck Ijon, and Dan, and Abel-beth-maacah, and all Chinneroth, namely, all the land of Naphtali.
verses.15:21: When Baasha heard this, he stopped building Ramah and returned to Tirzah.
verses.15:22: Then King Asa sent a message into all Judah, saying, "Let no one be excused." And they carried away the stones from Ramah and its timber, with which Baasha had built, and out of them King Asa constructed Geba of Benjamin and Mizpah.
verses.15:23: Now the rest of all the matters of Asa, and all his mighty deeds, and everything that he did, and the cities that he constructed, are these not written in the book of the words of the days of the kings of Judah? Nevertheless, in the time of his old age he suffered pain in his feet.
verses.15:24: And he slept with his fathers, and was buried with them in the city of David his father. And Jehoshaphat his son reigned in his place.
verses.15:25: Now Nadab son of Jeroboam reigned over Israel in the second year of Asa king of Judah; and he reigned over Israel for two years.
verses.15:26: And he did what is evil in the sight of the Lord, and walked in the ways of his father, and in his sins by which he caused Israel to sin.
verses.15:27: Now Baasha son of Ahijah, of the house of Issachar, conspired against him and struck him at Gibbethon, which is a city of the Philistines; for indeed Nadab and all Israel were besieging Gibbethon.
verses.15:28: Therefore Baasha killed him in the third year of Asa king of Judah, and reigned in his place.
verses.15:29: And when he had begun to reign, he struck the entire house of Jeroboam; he did not leave even a single soul of his seed until he destroyed him, according to the word of the Lord which He had spoken by the hand of His servant Ahijah the Shilonite,
verses.15:30: because of the sins of Jeroboam, which he had sinned and by which he had caused Israel to sin, and because of the offense by which he had provoked the Lord God of Israel.
verses.15:31: Now the rest of the matters of Nadab, and all that he performed, are these not written in the book of the words of the days of the kings of Israel?
verses.15:33: In the third year of Asa king of Judah, Baasha son of Ahijah reigned over all Israel in Tirzah for twenty-four years.
verses.15:34: And he did evil before the Lord, and walked in the way of Jeroboam, and in his sins by which he caused Israel to sin.
verses.16:1: Now the word of the Lord came to Jehu son of Hanani against Baasha, saying,
verses.16:2: "Because I exalted you from the dust and set you as leader over My people Israel, yet you walked in the way of Jeroboam and caused My people Israel to sin, so as to provoke Me by their sins,
verses.16:3: look, I will cut down the posterity of Baasha and the posterity of his house, and I will make your house like the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat.
verses.16:4: Anyone of Baasha who dies in the city, the dogs will eat him; and anyone of his who dies in the countryside, the birds of the sky will eat him."
verses.16:5: Now the rest of the matters of Baasha, and whatever he did, and his battles, are these not written in the book of the words of the days of the kings of Israel?
verses.16:6: So Baasha slept with his fathers and was buried in Tirzah, and Elah his son reigned in his place.
verses.16:7: Now when the word of the Lord had come by the hand of Jehu son of Hanani the prophet against Baasha and against his house, and against all the evil that he had done before the Lord, to provoke Him by the works of his hands, so that he would become like the house of Jeroboam, for this reason he killed him, that is, Jehu son of Hanani the prophet.
verses.16:8: In the twenty-sixth year of Asa king of Judah, Elah son of Baasha reigned over Israel in Tirzah for two years.
verses.16:9: And his servant Zimri, commander of half of the horsemen, rebelled against him; now Elah was in Tirzah, drinking and drunk in the house of Arza, the prefect of Tirzah.
verses.16:10: Rushing in, therefore, Zimri struck and killed him in the twenty-seventh year of Asa king of Judah, and reigned in his place.
verses.16:11: And when he had begun to reign and had sat upon his throne, he struck the entire house of Baasha, and did not leave from it one who urinates against a wall, nor his relatives or his friends.
verses.16:12: And Zimri destroyed the entire house of Baasha, according to the word of the Lord which He had spoken to Baasha by the hand of Jehu the prophet,
verses.16:13: because of all the sins of Baasha and the sins of Elah his son, who sinned and caused Israel to sin, provoking the Lord God of Israel by their vanities.
verses.16:14: Now the rest of the matters of Elah, and all that he did, are these not written in the book of the words of the days of the kings of Israel?
verses.16:15: In the twenty-seventh year of Asa king of Judah, Zimri reigned for seven days in Tirzah; meanwhile, the army was besieging Gibbethon, a city of the Philistines.
verses.16:16: And when they heard that Zimri had rebelled and had killed the king, all Israel made Omri, who was commander of the forces over Israel, king for themselves on that day in the camp.
verses.16:17: Therefore Omri, and all Israel with him, went up from Gibbethon, and they besieged Tirzah.
verses.16:18: Now Zimri, seeing that the city was about to be captured, entered the palace and set himself on fire along with the royal house; and he died
verses.16:19: in his sins which he had sinned, doing evil before the Lord and walking in the way of Jeroboam and in his sin by which he caused Israel to sin.
verses.16:20: Now the rest of the matters of Zimri, and of his conspiracy and tyranny, are these not written in the book of the words of the days of the kings of Israel?
verses.16:21: Then the people of Israel were divided into two parts: half of the people followed Tibni son of Ginath, to appoint him king, and half followed Omri.
verses.16:22: But the people who were with Omri prevailed over the people who followed Tibni son of Ginath; and Tibni died, and Omri reigned.
verses.16:23: In the thirty-first year of Asa king of Judah, Omri reigned over Israel for twelve years; in Tirzah he reigned for six years.
verses.16:24: And he bought the hill of Samaria from Shemer for two talents of silver, and built on it, and called the name of the city that he had constructed Samaria, after the name of Shemer, the owner of the hill.
verses.16:25: Now Omri did evil in the sight of the Lord, and acted wickedly more than all who were before him.
verses.16:26: And he walked in all the way of Jeroboam son of Nebat, and in his sins by which he had caused Israel to sin, so as to provoke the Lord God of Israel by his vanities.
verses.16:27: Now the rest of the matters of Omri, and his battles that he fought, are these not written in the book of the words of the days of the kings of Israel?
verses.16:28: And Omri slept with his fathers and was buried in Samaria; and Ahab his son reigned in his place. Moreover, he also removed from the land the remnant of the effeminate men who had remained in the days of Asa his father. And there was no king appointed in Edom at that time. Now King Jehoshaphat had made fleets on the sea to sail to Ophir for gold, yet they could not go, because they were shattered at Ezion-geber. Then Ahaziah son of Ahab said to Jehoshaphat, "Let my servants go with your servants in the ships." And Jehoshaphat was unwilling.
verses.16:29: Now Ahab son of Omri reigned over Israel in the thirty-eighth year of Asa king of Judah. And Ahab son of Omri reigned over Israel in Samaria for twenty-two years.
verses.16:30: And Ahab son of Omri did evil in the sight of the Lord more than all who were before him.
verses.16:31: Nor was it enough for him to walk in the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat; moreover, he took as wife Jezebel, daughter of Ethbaal king of the Sidonians. And he went and served Baal and worshiped him.
verses.16:32: And he set up an altar for Baal in the temple of Baal, which he had built in Samaria,
verses.16:33: and he planted a grove; and Ahab did yet more in his work, provoking the Lord God of Israel more than all the kings of Israel who were before him.
verses.16:34: In his days Hiel of Bethel built Jericho; in Abiram his firstborn he founded it, and in Segub his youngest he set its gates, according to the word of the Lord which He had spoken by the hand of Joshua son of Nun.
verses.17:1: And Elijah the Tishbite, of the inhabitants of Gilead, said to Ahab, "As the Lord God of Israel lives, in whose sight I stand, there will be no dew or rain during these years, except according to the words of my mouth."
verses.17:2: And the word of the Lord came to him, saying,
verses.17:3: "Depart from here, and go toward the east, and hide yourself at the stream Cherith, which is opposite the Jordan,
verses.17:4: and there you will drink from the stream; and I have commanded the ravens to feed you there."
verses.17:5: So he went and did according to the word of the Lord; and when he had gone, he settled at the stream Cherith, which is opposite the Jordan.
verses.17:6: The ravens also brought him bread and meat in the morning, and likewise bread and meat in the evening, and he drank from the stream.
verses.17:7: After some days, however, the stream dried up, for it had not rained upon the earth.
verses.17:8: Then the word of the Lord came to him, saying,
verses.17:9: "Rise and go to Zarephath of the Sidonians, and you will stay there; for I have commanded a widowed woman there to feed you."
verses.17:10: He rose and went to Zarephath. And when he had come to the gate of the city, a widowed woman appeared to him gathering wood; and he called to her and said to her, "Give me a little water in a vessel so that I may drink."
verses.17:11: And as she was going to bring it, he called out behind her back, saying, "Bring me, please, a morsel of bread in your hand as well."
verses.17:12: She answered, "As the Lord your God lives, I have no bread, except as much flour as a hand can hold in a jar, and a little oil in a flask. Look, I am gathering two pieces of wood so that I may go in and prepare it for myself and my son, so that we may eat and die."
verses.17:13: Elijah said to her, "Do not be afraid, but go and do as you have said; yet first make for me from that little bit of flour a small loaf baked under the ashes and bring it to me, and for yourself and your son you will make it afterward.
verses.17:14: For the Lord God of Israel says this: 'The jar of flour will not run out, nor will the flask of oil be reduced, until the day on which the Lord will give rain upon the face of the earth.'"
verses.17:15: So she went and did according to the word of Elijah; and he, she, and her household ate; and from that day
verses.17:16: the jar of flour did not run out, and the flask of oil was not reduced, according to the word of the Lord which He had spoken by the hand of Elijah.
verses.17:17: Now it happened after these things that the son of the woman, the mistress of the house, fell ill, and the illness was very severe, so that no breath remained in him.
verses.17:18: So she said to Elijah, "What is there between me and you, man of God? Have you come in to me so that my iniquities would be remembered and you would kill my son?"
verses.17:19: And Elijah said to her, "Give me your son." And he took him from her bosom, and carried him into the upper room where he himself was staying, and laid him on his own bed.
verses.17:20: And he cried out to the Lord and said, "Lord my God, have You also afflicted the widow with whom I am somehow sustained, so as to kill her son?"
verses.17:21: And he stretched himself out and measured himself over the boy three times, and cried out to the Lord and said, "Lord my God, please let the soul of this boy return into his inward parts."
verses.17:22: And the Lord heard the voice of Elijah, and the soul of the boy returned within him, and he lived again.
verses.17:23: And Elijah took the boy, and brought him down from the upper room into the lower part of the house, and gave him to his mother, and said to her, "Look, your son is alive."
verses.17:24: And the woman said to Elijah, "Now by this I know that you are a man of God, and the word of the Lord in your mouth is true."
verses.18:1: After many days the word of the Lord came to Elijah, in the third year, saying, "Go and show yourself to Ahab, so that I may give rain upon the face of the earth."
verses.18:2: So Elijah went to show himself to Ahab. Now there was a severe famine in Samaria.
verses.18:3: And Ahab called Obadiah, the steward of his house; now Obadiah feared the Lord greatly.
verses.18:4: For when Jezebel was killing the prophets of the Lord, he took one hundred prophets and hid them fifty by fifty in caves, and fed them with bread and water.
verses.18:5: So Ahab said to Obadiah, "Go into the land to all the springs of water and into all the valleys; perhaps we can find grass and save the horses and mules, so that the livestock do not completely perish."
verses.18:6: And they divided the regions between themselves to travel through them: Ahab went by one road, and Obadiah by the other road separately.
verses.18:7: And while Obadiah was on the road, Elijah met him; and when he recognized him, he fell upon his face and said, "Is it really you, my lord Elijah?"
verses.18:8: He answered him, "It is I. Go and say to your lord, 'Elijah is here.'"
verses.18:9: And he said, "How have I sinned, that you are handing me, your servant, over into the hand of Ahab so that he may kill me?
verses.18:10: As the Lord your God lives, there is no nation or kingdom where my lord has not sent seeking you; and when all answered, 'He is not here,' he made every individual kingdom and nation swear an oath because you were not found at all.
verses.18:11: And now you say to me, 'Go and say to your lord, "Elijah is here."'
verses.18:12: And when I have departed from you, the Spirit of the Lord will carry you away to a place that I do not know; and I will go in and report to Ahab, and when he does not find you, he will kill me; yet your servant has feared the Lord from his childhood.
verses.18:13: Has it not been reported to you, my lord, what I did when Jezebel was killing the prophets of the Lord, that I hid one hundred men of the prophets of the Lord, fifty by fifty, in caves, and fed them with bread and water?
verses.18:14: And now you say, 'Go and say to your lord, "Elijah is here,"' so that he may kill me?"
verses.18:15: And Elijah said, "As the Lord of hosts lives, before whose face I stand, today I will appear to him."
verses.18:16: So Obadiah went to meet Ahab and reported to him; and Ahab came to meet Elijah.
verses.18:17: And when he saw him, he said, "Are you the one who troubles Israel?"
verses.18:18: And he said, "I have not troubled Israel, but you and the house of your father, who have abandoned the commandments of the Lord and have followed the Baals.
verses.18:19: Yet now send and gather to me all Israel on Mount Carmel, and the four hundred fifty prophets of Baal, and the four hundred prophets of the groves, who eat from Jezebel's table."
verses.18:20: Ahab sent to all the sons of Israel and gathered the prophets on Mount Carmel.
verses.18:21: Now Elijah came near to all the people and said, "How long are you limping between two sides? If the Lord is God, follow Him; but if Baal, follow him." And the people did not answer him a word.
verses.18:22: And Elijah said again to the people, "I alone remain a prophet of the Lord, while the prophets of Baal are four hundred and fifty men.
verses.18:23: Let two bulls be given to us, and let them choose one bull for themselves, and cutting it into pieces let them lay it on the wood, but let them put no fire underneath; and I will prepare the other bull and place it on the wood, and I will put no fire underneath.
verses.18:24: Call upon the names of your gods, and I will call upon the name of my Lord; and the God who answers by fire, let Him be God." Answering, all the people said, "An excellent proposal."
verses.18:25: So Elijah said to the prophets of Baal, "Choose one bull for yourselves and prepare it first, because you are more numerous; and call upon the names of your gods, and put no fire underneath."
verses.18:26: When they had taken the bull that he had given them, they prepared it; and they called upon the name of Baal from morning until noon, saying, "Baal, answer us." Yet there was no voice, nor anyone who answered; and they kept leaping over the altar that they had made.
verses.18:27: And when it was already noon, Elijah mocked them, saying, "Shout with a louder voice, for he is a god; and perhaps he is talking, or he is at an inn, or on a journey, or surely he is asleep and must be awakened."
verses.18:28: So they shouted with a loud voice and cut themselves according to their custom with knives and lancets, until they were drenched with blood.
verses.18:29: Now after noon had passed, and while they were prophesying the time had come at which the sacrifice is customarily offered, and no voice was heard, nor did anyone answer, nor did anyone pay attention to those who were praying,
verses.18:30: Elijah said to all the people, "Come to me." And when the people approached him, he repaired the altar of the Lord that had been destroyed.
verses.18:31: And he took twelve stones according to the number of the tribes of the sons of Jacob, to whom the word of the Lord came, saying, "Israel will be your name."
verses.18:32: And from the stones he built an altar in the name of the Lord; and he made a water channel, about the space of two small furrows, around the altar,
verses.18:33: and arranged the wood, and divided the bull limb by limb, and laid it upon the wood,
verses.18:34: and said, "Fill four jars with water, and pour it over the burnt offering and over the wood." And again he said, "Do this a second time as well." When they had done it a second time, he said, "Do the very same thing a third time as well." And they did it a third time,
verses.18:35: and the waters ran around the altar, and the trench of the water channel was filled.
verses.18:36: And when it was now time for the burnt offering to be offered, Elijah the prophet came near and said, "Lord God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, show today that You are the God of Israel, and that I am Your servant, and that according to Your command I have done all these things.
verses.18:37: Answer me, Lord, answer me, so that this people may learn that You are the Lord God, and that You have turned their heart back again."
verses.18:38: Then the fire of the Lord fell and devoured the burnt offering, and the wood, and the stones, and the dust as well, licking up even the water that was in the water channel.
verses.18:39: When all the people saw this, they fell on their faces and said, "The Lord Himself is God! The Lord Himself is God!"
verses.18:40: And Elijah said to them, "Seize the prophets of Baal, and do not let even one of them escape." When they had seized them, Elijah led them to the stream Kishon and killed them there.
verses.18:41: And Elijah said to Ahab, "Go up, eat and drink, for there is the sound of heavy rain."
verses.18:42: Ahab went up to eat and drink, but Elijah went up to the summit of Carmel, and bowing down to the ground, he placed his face between his knees,
verses.18:43: and said to his servant, "Go up and look out toward the sea." When he had gone up and looked, he said, "There is nothing." And again he said to him, "Go back seven times."
verses.18:44: Now on the seventh time, look, a tiny cloud like a man's footprint was rising from the sea. And he said, "Go up and say to Ahab, 'Harness your chariot and go down, so that the rain does not overtake you.'"
verses.18:45: And as he turned this way and that, look, the skies grew dark, and there were clouds and wind, and a heavy rain fell. So Ahab mounted up and went to Jezreel,
verses.18:46: and the hand of the Lord came upon Elijah, and having girded his waist, he ran ahead of Ahab until he came to Jezreel.
verses.19:1: Now Ahab reported to Jezebel all that Elijah had done, and how he had killed all the prophets with the sword.
verses.19:2: And Jezebel sent a messenger to Elijah, saying, "May the gods do these things to me, and add these things, unless by this hour tomorrow I have made your life like the life of one of them."
verses.19:3: Therefore Elijah was afraid, and rising up, he went away wherever his will carried him; and he came to Beersheba of Judah and left his servant there.
verses.19:4: And he went on into the wilderness, a journey of one day. And when he had come and was sitting under a single juniper tree, he asked for his soul that he might die, and said, "It is enough for me, Lord; take my life, for I am no better than my fathers."
verses.19:5: And he threw himself down and fell asleep in the shade of the juniper tree; and look, an angel of the Lord touched him and said to him, "Rise and eat."
verses.19:6: He looked around, and look, at his head was bread baked under the ashes and a vessel of water. So he ate and drank, and fell asleep again.
verses.19:7: And the angel of the Lord returned a second time and touched him, and said to him, "Rise, eat, for a great journey remains for you."
verses.19:8: And when he had risen, he ate and drank, and walked in the strength of that food forty days and forty nights all the way to the mountain of God, Horeb.
verses.19:9: And when he had come there, he stayed in a cave; and look, the word of the Lord came to him, and He said to him, "What are you doing here, Elijah?"
verses.19:10: And he answered, "With zeal I have been zealous for the Lord God of hosts, because the sons of Israel have abandoned Your covenant; they have destroyed Your altars, they have killed Your prophets with the sword, I alone am left, and they are seeking my life to take it away."
verses.19:11: And He said to him, "Go out and stand on the mountain before the Lord." And look, the Lord was passing by; and a great and strong wind was overturning mountains and crushing rocks before the Lord; the Lord was not in the wind. And after the wind, a shaking; the Lord was not in the shaking.
verses.19:12: And after the shaking, a fire; the Lord was not in the fire. And after the fire, a whisper of a light breeze.
verses.19:13: And when Elijah had heard this, he covered his face with his cloak, and going out, he stood at the entrance of the cave. And look, a voice came to him, saying, "What are you doing here, Elijah?" And he answered:
verses.19:14: "With zeal I have been zealous for the Lord God of hosts, because the sons of Israel have abandoned Your covenant; they have destroyed Your altars, they have killed Your prophets with the sword, I alone am left, and they are seeking my life to take it away."
verses.19:15: And the Lord said to him, "Go and return on your way through the wilderness to Damascus; and when you arrive there, you will anoint Hazael king over Syria,
verses.19:16: and you will anoint Jehu the son of Nimshi king over Israel; and you will anoint Elisha the son of Shaphat, who is from Abel-meholah, as prophet in your place.
verses.19:17: And it will be: whoever escapes the sword of Hazael, Jehu will kill him; and whoever escapes the sword of Jehu, Elisha will put him to death.
verses.19:18: And I will leave for Myself in Israel seven thousand men, whose knees have not been bowed before Baal, and every mouth that has not worshiped him by kissing the hands."
verses.19:19: So departing from there, Elijah found Elisha the son of Shaphat plowing with twelve yokes of oxen. And he himself was one among the twelve yokes of oxen that were plowing; and when Elijah had come to him, he threw his cloak over him.
verses.19:20: And immediately, leaving the oxen, he ran after Elijah and said, "Please let me kiss my father and my mother, and then I will follow you." And he said to him, "Go and return, for what was mine, I have done to you."
verses.19:21: And returning from him, he took a pair of oxen and slaughtered them, and with the plow of the oxen he cooked the meat and gave it to the people, and they ate; and rising up, he went away and followed Elijah, and served him.
verses.20:1: Now after these things, at that time, there was a vineyard belonging to Naboth the Jezreelite, which was in Jezreel, beside the palace of Ahab king of Samaria.
verses.20:2: So Ahab spoke to Naboth, saying, "Give me your vineyard, so that I may make for myself a vegetable garden, because it is nearby and close to my house; and I will give you a better vineyard for it, or if you consider it more convenient for you, the price in silver, as much as it is worth."
verses.20:3: And Naboth answered him, "May the Lord be merciful to me, so that I do not give the inheritance of my fathers to you."
verses.20:4: So Ahab came into his house indignant and gnashing his teeth over the word that Naboth the Jezreelite had spoken to him, saying, "I will not give you the inheritance of my fathers." And throwing himself onto his bed, he turned his face toward the wall and did not eat bread.
verses.20:5: Now Jezebel his wife came in to him and said to him, "What is this, from which your soul is saddened? And why are you not eating bread?"
verses.20:6: And he answered her, "I spoke to Naboth the Jezreelite and said to him, 'Give me your vineyard on receiving money, or, if it pleases you, I will give you a better vineyard for it.' And he said, 'I will not give you my vineyard.'"
verses.20:7: Then Jezebel his wife said to him, "You are of great authority, and you rule the kingdom of Israel well. Rise and eat bread, and be of a calm mind; I myself will give you the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite."
verses.20:8: Accordingly, she wrote letters in the name of Ahab, and sealed them with his ring, and sent them to the elders and nobles who were in his city and lived with Naboth.
verses.20:9: Now this was the message of the letters: "Proclaim a fast, and have Naboth sit among the foremost of the people,
verses.20:10: and set two men, sons of Belial, against him, and let them speak false testimony, 'He has blessed God and the king,' and lead him out and stone him, and so let him die."
verses.20:11: So his fellow citizens, the elders and nobles who lived with him in the city, did just as Jezebel had commanded them, and just as it was written in the letters that she had sent to them.
verses.20:12: They proclaimed a fast, and had Naboth sit among the foremost of the people.
verses.20:13: And having brought in two men, sons of the devil, they had them sit opposite him; and they, indeed as diabolical men, spoke testimony against him before the multitude: "Naboth has blessed God and the king." For this reason they led him outside the city and put him to death with stones.
verses.20:14: And they sent word to Jezebel, saying, "Naboth has been stoned and is dead."
verses.20:15: Now it happened, when Jezebel heard that Naboth had been stoned and was dead, that she spoke to Ahab, "Rise and take possession of the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite, who refused to agree with you and give it on receiving money; for Naboth is not alive, but is dead."
verses.20:16: And when Ahab heard this, namely, that Naboth was dead, he rose and was going down to the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite to take possession of it.
verses.20:17: Therefore the word of the Lord came to Elijah the Tishbite, saying:
verses.20:18: "Rise and go down to meet Ahab king of Israel, who is in Samaria; look, he is going down to the vineyard of Naboth to take possession of it.
verses.20:19: And you will speak to him, saying, 'This is what the Lord says: You have killed, and moreover you have taken possession.' And after these things you will add, 'This is what the Lord says: In this place in which dogs licked the blood of Naboth, they will also lick your blood.'"
verses.20:20: And Ahab said to Elijah, "Have you found me an enemy to you?" And he said, "I have found you, because you have been sold to do evil in the sight of the Lord.
verses.20:21: Look, I will bring evil upon you, and I will cut down your posterity, and I will put to death from Ahab anyone who urinates against the wall, both the confined and the last in Israel.
verses.20:22: And I will make your house like the house of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, and like the house of Baasha the son of Ahijah, because you have acted to provoke Me to anger and have made Israel sin.
verses.20:23: And concerning Jezebel also the Lord has spoken, saying, 'Dogs will eat Jezebel in the field of Jezreel.
verses.20:24: If Ahab dies in the city, dogs will eat him; but if he dies in the field, the birds of the sky will eat him.'"
verses.20:25: Therefore there was no one else like Ahab, who was sold to do evil in the sight of the Lord, for Jezebel his wife incited him.
verses.20:26: And he became abominable, to such an extent that he followed the idols that the Amorites had made, whom the Lord consumed from before the face of the sons of Israel.
verses.20:27: And so, when Ahab heard these words, he tore his garments and covered his flesh with haircloth, and fasted and slept in sackcloth, and walked with his head bowed.
verses.20:28: And the word of the Lord came to Elijah the Tishbite, saying:
verses.20:29: "Have you not seen Ahab humbled before Me? Therefore, because he has humbled himself on My account, I will not bring evil in his days, but in the days of his son I will bring evil upon his house."
verses.21:1: Now Ben-hadad, king of Syria, gathered his entire army, and thirty-two kings with him, and horses and chariots; and going up, he was fighting against Samaria and besieging it.
verses.21:2: And sending messengers to Ahab, king of Israel, into the city,
verses.21:3: he said, "This is what Ben-hadad says: Your silver and your gold are mine, and your wives and your best sons are mine."
verses.21:4: And the king of Israel answered, "According to your word, my lord the king, I am yours, and all that is mine."
verses.21:5: And returning, the messengers said, "This is what Ben-hadad, who sent us to you, says: Your silver and your gold, and your wives and your sons, you will give to me.
verses.21:6: Therefore tomorrow at this same hour I will send my servants to you, and they will search your house and the house of your servants; and everything that pleases them they will put in their hands and carry away."
verses.21:7: Now the king of Israel called all the elders of the land and said, "Take notice and see that he is plotting against us; for he sent to me for my wives and sons, and for silver and gold, and I did not refuse."
verses.21:8: And all the elders and the entire people said to him, "Do not listen, nor consent to him."
verses.21:9: Therefore he answered the messengers of Ben-hadad, "Say to my lord the king, 'Everything for which you sent to me, your servant, at the beginning, I will do; but this thing I cannot do.'"
verses.21:10: And the messengers returned and reported to him. And he sent back and said, "May the gods do these things to me, and add these things as well, if the dust of Samaria suffices for handfuls for all the people who follow me."
verses.21:11: And answering, the king of Israel said, "Tell him, 'Do not let the one who has fastened his belt boast equally with the one who has unfastened it.'"
verses.21:12: Now it happened, when Ben-hadad had heard this word, that he himself and the kings were drinking in the pavilions, and he said to his servants, "Surround the city." And they surrounded it.
verses.21:13: And look, a certain prophet, approaching Ahab, king of Israel, said to him, "This is what the Lord says: Surely you have seen all this vast multitude? Look, I will deliver it into your hand today, so that you may know that I am the Lord."
verses.21:14: And Ahab said, "By whom?" And he said to him, "This is what the Lord says: By the attendants of the governors of the provinces." And he said, "Who will begin to do battle?" And he said, "You."
verses.21:15: Therefore he mustered the young men of the governors of the provinces, and found the number to be two hundred thirty-two; and after them he mustered the people, all the sons of Israel, seven thousand.
verses.21:16: And they went out at noon. Now Ben-hadad was drinking, drunk, in his pavilion, and the thirty-two kings with him, who had come to his aid.
verses.21:17: Now the young men of the governors of the provinces went out in the front line. Therefore Ben-hadad sent out, and they reported to him, saying, "Men have come out from Samaria."
verses.21:18: And he said, "Whether they are coming for peace, seize them alive; or whether to do battle, capture them alive."
verses.21:19: Therefore the young men of the governors of the provinces went out, and the rest of the army was following;
verses.21:20: and each one struck down the man who was coming against him; and the Syrians fled, and Israel pursued them. Ben-hadad, king of Syria, also fled on a horse with his horsemen.
verses.21:21: Moreover, the king of Israel went out and struck the horses and chariots, and he struck Syria with a great blow.
verses.21:22: Now the prophet, approaching the king of Israel, said to him, "Go and strengthen yourself, and know and see what you should do; for in the following year the king of Syria will go up against you."
verses.21:23: But the servants of the king of Syria said to him, "Gods of the mountains are their gods; therefore they overpowered us; yet it is better that we fight against them on the plains, and we will prevail over them.
verses.21:24: You therefore do this thing: remove each of the kings from your army, and place governors in their place,
verses.21:25: and restore the number of soldiers who fell from yours, and horses like the former horses, and chariots like the chariots that you had before; and we will fight against them on the plains, and you will see that we will prevail over them." He believed their counsel and did so.
verses.21:26: Therefore, after a year had passed, Ben-hadad mustered the Syrians and went up to Aphek to fight against Israel.
verses.21:27: Now the sons of Israel were mustered, and having received provisions, they set out opposite them and pitched camp against them like two small flocks of goats; but the Syrians filled the land.
verses.21:28: (And approaching, a certain man of God said to the king of Israel, "This is what the Lord says: Because the Syrians have said, 'The Lord is a God of the mountains, and is not a God of the valleys,' I will give all this great multitude into your hand, and you will know that I am the Lord.")
verses.21:29: And for seven days both sides were drawing up battle lines opposite each other, but on the seventh day battle was joined; and the sons of Israel struck down one hundred thousand foot soldiers of the Syrians in one day.
verses.21:30: Now those who had remained fled into Aphek, into the city; and the wall fell upon twenty-seven thousand men who had remained. Meanwhile Ben-hadad, fleeing, entered the city, into a chamber that was inside a chamber.
verses.21:31: And his servants said to him, "Look, we have heard that the kings of the house of Israel are merciful. Therefore let us put sackcloth around our waists and ropes on our heads, and let us go out to the king of Israel; perhaps he will save our lives."
verses.21:32: They bound sackcloth around their waists and put ropes on their heads, and came to the king of Israel and said to him, "Your servant Ben-hadad says, 'Let my soul live, I beg you.'" And he said, "If he is still alive, he is my brother."
verses.21:33: And the men took this as an omen; and hurrying, they snatched the word from his mouth and said, "Your brother Ben-hadad." And he said to them, "Go and bring him to me." Therefore Ben-hadad came out to him, and he lifted him up into his chariot.
verses.21:34: And he said to him, "The cities that my father took from your father I will return, and make streets for yourself in Damascus, just as my father did in Samaria; and I, bound by a treaty, will depart from you." Therefore he made a treaty and let him go.
verses.21:35: Then a certain man of the sons of the prophets said to his companion by the word of the Lord, "Strike me." But he refused to strike.
verses.21:36: And he said to him, "Because you refused to listen to the voice of the Lord, look, you will depart from me, and a lion will strike you." And when he had departed a little way from him, a lion found him and struck him.
verses.21:37: And finding another man as well, he said to him, "Strike me." And he struck him and wounded him.
verses.21:38: Therefore the prophet went off and met the king on the road, and he altered his face and his eyes by a sprinkling of dust.
verses.21:39: And when the king had passed by, he cried out to the king and said, "Your servant went out to do battle at close quarters; and when one man had fled, someone brought him to me and said, 'Guard this man; if he slips away, your life will be for his life, or you will weigh out a talent of silver.'
verses.21:40: Now while I, distracted, was turning this way and that, suddenly he disappeared." And the king of Israel said to him, "This is your judgment, which you yourself have decreed."
verses.21:41: But he immediately wiped the dust from his face, and the king of Israel recognized him, that he was one of the prophets.
verses.21:42: And he said to him, "This is what the Lord says: Because you have let a man worthy of death go from your hand, your life will be for his life, and your people for his people."
verses.21:43: Therefore the king of Israel returned to his house, scorning to listen, and came into Samaria furious.
verses.22:1: So three years passed without war between Syria and Israel.
verses.22:2: Now in the third year, Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, went down to the king of Israel.
verses.22:3: And the king of Israel said to his servants, "Do you not know that Ramoth-Gilead is ours, and we neglect to take it from the hand of the king of Syria?"
verses.22:4: And he said to Jehoshaphat, "Will you come with me to fight at Ramoth-Gilead?"
verses.22:5: And Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel, "As I am, so also are you; my people and your people are one, and my horsemen are your horsemen." And Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel, "Seek, I ask you, the word of the Lord today."
verses.22:6: Therefore the king of Israel gathered the prophets, about four hundred men, and said to them, "Should I go to Ramoth-Gilead to wage war, or remain still?" And they answered, "Go up, and the Lord will give it into the hand of the king."
verses.22:7: But Jehoshaphat said, "Is there not some prophet of the Lord here, so that we may inquire through him?"
verses.22:8: And the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "There remains one man through whom we can inquire of the Lord, but I hate him, because he does not prophesy good for me, but evil: Micaiah, son of Imlah." And Jehoshaphat said to him, "Do not speak like that, king."
verses.22:9: Therefore the king of Israel called a certain eunuch and said to him, "Hurry to bring Micaiah, son of Imlah."
verses.22:10: Now the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, were each sitting on his own throne, dressed in royal attire, on a threshing floor next to the entrance of the gate of Samaria, and all the prophets were prophesying in their sight.
verses.22:11: Zedekiah, son of Chenaanah, also made iron horns for himself and said, "This is what the Lord says: 'With these you will toss Syria until you destroy it.'"
verses.22:12: And all the prophets were prophesying likewise, saying, "Go up to Ramoth-Gilead, and go prosperously, and the Lord will deliver it into the hands of the king."
verses.22:13: Now the messenger who had gone to call Micaiah spoke to him, saying, "Look, the words of the prophets with one mouth proclaim good things to the king; therefore let your word be like theirs, and speak good things."
verses.22:14: And Micaiah said to him, "As the Lord lives, whatever the Lord says to me, this I will speak."
verses.22:15: So he came to the king, and the king said to him, "Micaiah, should we go to Ramoth-Gilead to fight, or refrain?" And he answered him, "Go up, and go prosperously, and the Lord will deliver it into the hands of the king."
verses.22:16: But the king said to him, "Again and again I adjure you to speak to me nothing except what is true, in the name of the Lord."
verses.22:17: And he said, "I saw all Israel scattered on the mountains, like sheep having no shepherd. And the Lord said, 'These have no master; let each one return to his own house in peace.'"
verses.22:18: Therefore the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "Did I not tell you that he does not prophesy good for me, but always evil?"
verses.22:19: But he continued and said, "Therefore, hear the word of the Lord: I saw the Lord sitting upon His throne, and all the host of heaven standing beside Him on the right and on the left,
verses.22:20: and the Lord said, 'Who will deceive Ahab, king of Israel, so that he may go up and fall at Ramoth-Gilead?' And one spoke words of this kind, and another differently.
verses.22:21: Then a spirit came out and stood before the Lord, and said, 'I will deceive him.' And the Lord spoke to him, 'By what means?'
verses.22:22: And he said, 'I will go out, and I will be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets.' And the Lord said, 'You will deceive, and you will prevail; go out and do so.'
verses.22:23: Now therefore, look, the Lord has put a spirit of lying in the mouth of all your prophets who are here, and the Lord has spoken evil against you."
verses.22:24: Then Zedekiah, son of Chenaanah, approached and struck Micaiah on the cheek, and said, "Has the Spirit of the Lord then left me and spoken to you?"
verses.22:25: And Micaiah said, "You will see on that day when you enter a room within a room to hide yourself."
verses.22:26: And the king of Israel said, "Take Micaiah, and let him remain with Amon, the governor of the city, and with Joash, son of Amelech,
verses.22:27: and say to them, 'This is what the king says: Put this man in prison, and sustain him with bread of affliction and water of distress, until I return in peace.'"
verses.22:28: And Micaiah said, "If you return in peace, the Lord has not spoken in me." And he said, "Hear, all peoples."
verses.22:29: So the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, went up to Ramoth-Gilead.
verses.22:30: So the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "Take up arms, and enter the battle, and put on your own garments." Meanwhile, the king of Israel changed his attire and entered the war.
verses.22:31: Now the king of Syria had commanded the thirty-two commanders of the chariots, saying, "You are not to fight against anyone small or great, except against the king of Israel alone."
verses.22:32: Therefore, when the commanders of the chariots saw Jehoshaphat, they suspected that he was the king of Israel, and making a charge, they began fighting against him; and Jehoshaphat cried out.
verses.22:33: And the commanders of the chariots realized that he was not the king of Israel, and they broke off from him.
verses.22:34: Now a certain man drew a bow, aiming an arrow at random, and by chance struck the king of Israel between the lung and the stomach. And he said to his charioteer, "Turn your hand and bring me out of the army, for I am severely wounded."
verses.22:35: So the battle was joined on that day, and the king of Israel was standing in his chariot facing the Syrians, and he died in the evening; and the blood of the wound was flowing into the hollow of the chariot.
verses.22:36: And a herald called out throughout the entire army before the sun set, saying, "Let each one return to his city and to his own land."
verses.22:37: Now the king died and was brought to Samaria, and they buried the king in Samaria.
verses.22:38: And they washed his chariot in the pool of Samaria, and the dogs licked his blood, and they washed the reins, according to the word of the Lord which He had spoken.
verses.22:39: Now the rest of the accounts of Ahab, and everything that he did, and the ivory house that he built, and all the cities that he constructed, are these not written in the book of the accounts of the days of the kings of Israel?
verses.22:40: So Ahab slept with his fathers, and Ahaziah his son reigned in his place.
verses.22:41: Now Jehoshaphat, son of Asa, had begun to reign over Judah in the fourth year of Ahab, king of Israel.
verses.22:42: He was thirty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned twenty-five years in Jerusalem; the name of his mother was Azubah, daughter of Shilhi.
verses.22:43: And he walked in the entire way of Asa his father, and did not turn aside from it; and he did what was right in the sight of the Lord.
verses.22:44: Nevertheless, he did not remove the high places, for the people were still sacrificing and burning incense on the high places.
verses.22:45: And Jehoshaphat had peace with the king of Israel.
verses.22:46: Now the rest of the matters of Jehoshaphat, and his works that he performed, and the battles, are these not written in the book of the words of the days of the kings of Judah?
verses.22:51: And Jehoshaphat slept with his fathers, and was buried with them in the city of David his father; and Jehoram his son reigned in his place.
verses.22:52: Now Ahaziah, son of Ahab, had begun to reign over Israel in Samaria in the seventeenth year of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, and he reigned over Israel for two years.
verses.22:53: And he did evil in the sight of the Lord, and walked in the way of his father and of his mother, and in the way of Jeroboam, son of Nebat, who made Israel sin.
verses.22:54: He also served Baal and worshiped him, and he provoked the Lord God of Israel, according to all that his father had done.

notes.1:4: Vulgate "and she slept with the king" (dormiebatque cum rege) is a distinctive Latin rendering where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "and she became an attendant to the king" and the Septuagint reads "she was warming him."
notes.1:21: Latin "peccatores" ("sinners") literally preserves the biblical idiom for being regarded as guilty offenders or traitors.
notes.1:40: Vulgate "insonuit terra" ("the earth resounded") differs from the Hebrew Masoretic Text, which has "the earth split open" from their sound.
notes.1:47: The Clementine Vulgate prints the active verb "magnificet" with the nominative "thronus ejus" (a blend of "magnificet thronum" and passive "magnificetur thronus"); here God is kept as the subject of both verbs.
notes.1:50: The Vulgate reads the singular "cornu altaris" ("the horn of the altar," also in 1:51), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text has the plural "horns of the altar."
notes.2:3: The Vulgate renders the Hebrew verb for prospering or acting wisely as ut intelligas ("so that you may understand") and translates Hebrew "statutes" as caeremonias ("ceremonies").
notes.2:6: Latin ad inferos ("to the underworld," here and in 2:9) denotes the lower world or abode of the dead, corresponding to Hebrew Sheol.
notes.2:8: The Vulgate renders Hebrew ben-hayemini ("the Benjaminite") literally as a patronymic, "the son of Jemini," and translates the place name Mahanaim by its literal meaning, "the camp" (ad castra).
notes.2:35: The Clementine Vulgate retains this closing summary of Solomon's five hundred and fifty chief officers, thrice-yearly sacrifices, and the completion of the temple, reflecting an ancient textual tradition paralleled in the Septuagint miscellanies and in 1 Kings 9:23, 25 but absent here in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.2:46: The Clementine Vulgate appends a summary of Solomon's prosperous reign (paralleling 1 Kings 4:20-21, 25 in the Hebrew text and the Septuagint miscellany at 2:46) and reads a flumine terrae Philisthiim ("from the river of the land of the Philistines"), where Hebrew 4:21 reads "from the River [Euphrates] to the land of the Philistines."
notes.3:8: Latin populi infiniti ("a boundless people") is a distinctive Vulgate rendering where the Hebrew reads "a great/numerous people."
notes.3:9: Latin cor docile literally means "a teachable heart," differing from the Hebrew idiom "a listening heart"; Dabis is literally future indicative ("You will give") used with the force of a petition.
notes.3:13: Latin cunctis retro diebus ("in all past days") is a distinctive Vulgate reading comparing Solomon to all earlier kings, whereas the Hebrew reads "all your days."
notes.3:17: Latin in cubiculo specifies "in the bedroom" (or chamber), whereas the Hebrew reads "in the house."
notes.3:22: Latin Mentiris ("You are lying!") is a distinctive Vulgate expansion where the Hebrew simply reads "No."
notes.4:2: Latin places sacerdotis ("the priest") in the genitive modifying Zadok ("the son of Zadok the priest"), whereas the Hebrew is commonly read as designating Azariah himself as the priest.
notes.4:5: Latin super eos qui assistebant regi ("over those who attended the king") interprets the office as royal attendants rather than the Hebrew "over the officers/deputies."
notes.4:6: Latin super tributa ("over the tributes") renders the office as overseeing taxation/tribute rather than the Hebrew "over the forced labor."
notes.4:13: Latin transliterates Hebrew Chavvot-Jair ("the tent-villages of Jair") as a single name Avothjair, followed by the genitive filii Manasse ("of the son of Manasseh").
notes.4:18: The Clementine Vulgate orders 4:17-19 differently from the Hebrew Masoretic Text (Vulgate 4:17, 4:18, 4:19 correspond to Hebrew 4:18, 4:19, 4:17). Moreover, Latin super omnia quae erant in illa terra ("over all things that were in that land") is a distinctive Vulgate reading where the Hebrew reads "and he was the only officer in the land."
notes.5:17: The Vulgate reads 'voluntatem David patris mei' ('the will of David my father'), explicitly supplying 'will' where the Hebrew Masoretic Text simply reads 'You know David my father, that he could not build.'
notes.5:18: Latin retains the transliterated Hebrew common noun 'satan' here in its basic sense of 'adversary' or 'opponent,' paired with 'occursus malus' ('evil encounter').
notes.5:23: The Vulgate renders the verb as 'applicabo' ('I will bring ashore' or 'land'), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads 'I will break them apart' (that is, disassemble the rafts).
notes.5:32: Latin opens with the relative pronoun 'quos' ('these' or 'which'), referring to the great foundation stones whose cutting appears at the beginning of 6:1 in this chapter arrangement.
notes.6:1: The Clementine Vulgate spells the second month 'Zio' (a manuscript variant of 'Ziu' for Hebrew 'Ziv'), agrees with the Hebrew Masoretic Text in reading the 'four hundred and eightieth' year (Septuagint: 'four hundred and fortieth'), and renders 'in universis utensilibus suis' ('in all its utensils') where the Hebrew reads 'in all its specifications.'
notes.6:4: Latin 'fenestras obliquas' ('oblique windows') interprets the debated Hebrew architectural phrase as splayed or slanted embrasure windows cut through the thick temple wall.
notes.6:5: Throughout chapter 6, the Vulgate renders the inner sanctuary (Hebrew 'debir') as 'oraculum' ('oracle'), connecting it etymologically with the Hebrew root for speaking as the chamber of divine utterance.
notes.6:6: The Vulgate reads 'trabes' ('beams') placed around the outside of the house, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text refers to stepped ledges or offsets cut into the outer temple wall.
notes.6:21: The Vulgate reads 'affixit laminas clavis aureis' ('fastened the plates with golden nails'), diverging from the Hebrew Masoretic Text, which speaks of drawing golden chains across in front of the inner sanctuary.
notes.7:9: The Vulgate reads malogranatorum autem ducenti ordines ("two hundred rows of pomegranates") around the second capital, whereas the Hebrew describes two hundred pomegranates arranged in rows.
notes.7:11: The Vulgate renders the border ornament as fluted carvings (sculpturarum striatarum) encompassing the sea for ten cubits (decem cubitis), where the Hebrew speaks of gourds set ten to a cubit.
notes.7:27: Latin funiculos capitellorum ("cords of the capitals") is a distinctive Vulgate rendering where the Hebrew refers to bowl-shaped globes on the capitals.
notes.7:31: This difficult architectural verse preserves the Vulgate's distinctive phrasing, including in angulis columnarum ("at the corners of the pillars") and media intercolumnia ("the middle spaces between the pillars").
notes.7:35: Latin oraculum ("oracle") is the Vulgate's standard term for the inner sanctuary (the Holy of Holies) where the Lord spoke.
notes.8:6: Latin oraculum ("oracle," also in 8:8) renders the inner sanctuary as the place of divine speech, reflecting Jerome's etymological translation of Hebrew debir.
notes.8:8: Latin foris sanctuarium literally reads "outside the sanctuary," differing from the Hebrew Masoretic Text ("from the Holy Place").
notes.8:15: Latin literally reads in manibus ejus ("in/with his hands"), using the non-reflexive pronoun ejus and plural manibus; the context and the parallel in 8:24 indicate God's own hands, though some Latin readers have linked ejus to David.
notes.8:28: Latin hymnum ("hymn") is a distinctly Vulgate rendering where the Hebrew has "cry" or "ringing cry."
notes.8:33: Latin distinctively reads fugerit inimicos suos ("flee from their enemies"), the future periphrastic quia peccaturus est tibi ("because they will sin against You"), and agentes poenitentiam ("doing penance"), whereas the Hebrew has "are defeated before an enemy because they have sinned against You, and turn back to You."
notes.8:38: Latin devotatio et imprecatio quae acciderit ("curse and imprecation that happens to") is a distinctly Vulgate reading where the Hebrew has "any prayer or plea" offered by anyone.
notes.8:43: Latin in firmamento habitaculi tui (and in firmamento solii tui in 8:49) uses firmamentum ("foundation/firm support"), with 8:49 distinctively specifying "Your throne" (solii tui) rather than "Your dwelling."
notes.8:53: The Saints Latin Critical Text places Solomon's declaration ("Then Solomon said: The Lord said that He would dwell in a cloud...") at the opening of 8:53 rather than at 8:12-13.
notes.8:61: Latin uses the first-person plural (cor nostrum, ambulemus, custodiamus -- "our heart ... we may walk ... keep"), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text addresses the assembly in the second-person plural ("your heart").
notes.9:8: The Vulgate reads "will become an example" (in exemplum), portraying the ruined house as a cautionary sign, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "will be high" (often understood or emended as "a heap of ruins").
notes.9:9: The notice of Pharaoh's daughter moving into her house and the building of Millo stands here in the Saints Latin Critical Text (matching the Septuagint 3 Kingdoms arrangement) rather than at 9:24 as in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.10:5: The Vulgate renders Hebrew "seating" as "dwellings" (habitacula) and reads "burnt offerings" (holocausta) rather than "ascent" or "stairway," reflecting a well-known ambiguity in the Hebrew consonantal text.
notes.10:11: Latin "ligna thyina" ("thyine wood," an aromatic North African conifer timber) is the Vulgate rendering of Hebrew "almug wood."
notes.10:17: The Vulgate reads "three hundred minas" (trecentæ minæ), matching the number three hundred in 2 Chronicles 9:16 and several Septuagint witnesses, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text of 1 Kings reads "three minas."
notes.10:22: Following the Septuagint 3 Kingdoms order, this verse incorporates the account of Solomon's building projects and tribute labor (placed at 9:15, 17-22 in the Masoretic Text) before the "For the king's fleet" (quia) clause continuing 10:21. Distinctively Vulgate readings include "sum of the expenses" (summa expensarum) for Hebrew "forced labor," "villages... without a wall" for "storage cities," and "Palmyra" (Palmiram) for Hebrew Tamar/Tadmor.
notes.10:26: The opening sentence on Solomon's forty thousand stalls for chariot horses and twelve thousand riding horses stands here following the Septuagint 3 Kingdoms placement (compare 1 Kings 4:26 in the Hebrew text), and the Vulgate reads "fortified cities" (civitates munitas) where the Hebrew has "chariot cities."
notes.10:29: The Vulgate states that the kings of the Hittites and of Syria "sold horses" (equos venundabant), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text describes Solomon's merchants exporting horses and chariots to those kings.
notes.11:1: Following the 3 Kingdoms sequence, the count of Solomon's wives and concubines (traditionally v. 3) is included here before v. 2. The Vulgate also reads "also the daughter of Pharaoh" (filiam quoque Pharaonis) and "wives as queens" (uxores quasi reginæ).
notes.11:5: Following the 3 Kingdoms order, the building of the shrines precedes the summary of Solomon's worship in v. 6. The Vulgate reads "Molech" (Moloch) here and in vv. 6 and 33, where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads Milcom in vv. 5 and 33.
notes.11:14: The account of Rezon (traditionally vv. 23-24) is placed directly after Hadad's introduction, matching the 3 Kingdoms arrangement. The Vulgate also reads "gathered men against him" (congregavit contra eum viros) rather than "to himself."
notes.11:25: Because vv. 23-24 appear in v. 14, this verse directly follows Hadad's departure. The Vulgate distinctively reads "and this is the evil of Hadad, and the hatred against Israel; and he reigned in Syria."
notes.11:43: Jeroboam's return from Egypt upon hearing of Solomon's death (traditionally 12:2) is placed at the end of ch. 11 in accordance with the 3 Kingdoms sequence, while traditional 11:39 is absent.
notes.12:10: The Vulgate reads "the back of my father" (dorso patris mei), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "my father's loins" or "waist."
notes.12:15: The Vulgate reads "because the Lord had turned away from him" (quoniam aversatus fuerat eum Dominus), where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "for it was a turn of affairs from the LORD."
notes.12:24: Following the 3 Kingdoms supplement (12:24g-n), this verse includes the narrative of Abijah's illness and Ahijah's prophecy (paralleling 1 Kings 14:1-6, 10-13, 17-18). Within it, the Vulgate distinctively reads "both the confined and the last" (et clausum, et novissimum) and "a good word from the Lord God of Israel" (sermo bonus a Domino Deo Israël).
notes.12:30: The Vulgate explicitly reads "to worship the calf" (ad adorandum vitulum) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "before the one," and in v. 31 renders the origin of the priests as "from the lowest of the people" (de extremis populi).
notes.13:6: Latin "Deprecare faciem Domini" ("implore the face of the Lord") and "oravit faciem Domini" ("prayed to the face of the Lord") preserve a literal Hebrew idiom for seeking God's favor.
notes.13:12: Latin "Ostenderunt ei filii sui" ("His sons showed him") agrees with the Septuagint vocalization against the Hebrew Masoretic Text ("his sons had seen"), and Latin uses plural "filii" throughout vv. 11-12.
notes.13:17: Latin "locutus est Dominus ad me in sermone Domini" explicitly states "the Lord spoke to me by the word of the Lord," where the Hebrew has an impersonal passive ("it was said to me by the word of the Lord").
notes.13:29: Latin ends with "ut plangeret eum" ("to mourn him") alone, without the additional phrase "and to bury him" found in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.13:33: Latin "de novissimis populi" ("from the lowest of the people") interprets Hebrew "from all sorts of people," and "implebat manum suam" ("filled his hand") reflects the biblical idiom for priestly consecration, with the implied subject understood either as the applicant or Jeroboam.
notes.14:23: The Vulgate renders the three Hebrew cultic terms (high places, sacred pillars, and Asherah poles) as "aras" ("altars"), "statuas" ("statues"), and "lucos" ("groves").
notes.14:24: Latin "effeminati" ("effeminate men") renders the Hebrew term for a male cult prostitute, and "attrivit" ("crushed") corresponds to Hebrew "drove out."
notes.14:27: Latin "scutariorum" ("shield-bearers," also in v. 28 with "those who had the duty of going ahead" and "armory") renders the Hebrew royal guard ("runners") and their guardroom.
notes.14:29: Latin "ecce scripta sunt" ("look, they are written") is declarative rather than the Hebrew rhetorical question ("are they not written?"), and "sermonum" and "libro sermonum dierum" literally reproduce the Hebrew idioms for royal acts and annals.
notes.15:7: Verse 6 is absent in this Clementine Vulgate text, with the battle notice between Abijam and Jeroboam appearing at the end of verse 7. The Vulgate's 'book of the words of the days' (in libro verborum dierum) literally reflects the Hebrew title for the royal annals or chronicles.
notes.15:12: The Vulgate renders the Hebrew term for male cult prostitutes (qedeshim) as 'effeminate men' (effeminatos), a rendering repeated in 16:28.
notes.15:13: Distinctly Vulgate reading: Jerome interpreted the Hebrew 'horrid image for Asherah' in terms of the Greco-Roman fertility god Priapus ('in the sacred rites of Priapus', in sacris Priapi), rendering Asherah as 'grove' (luco) and adding 'his cavern' (specum ejus) and 'the most shameful image' (simulacrum turpissimum).
notes.15:20: The Vulgate half-translates the place name Abel-beth-maacah as Abeldomum Maacha ('Abel-house of Maacah') and inserts 'namely' (scilicet) to equate all Chinneroth with all the land of Naphtali.
notes.15:31: Verse 32 (which in the Hebrew repeats the war notice between Asa and Baasha from verse 16) is absent from this Clementine Vulgate text.
notes.16:3: The Vulgate renders the Hebrew threat to sweep away Baasha's house with the agricultural metaphor 'cut down the posterity' (demetam posteriora).
notes.16:7: Striking Vulgate-distinct reading: whereas the Hebrew cites Baasha's slaughter of Jeroboam's house as a reason for the oracle, the Clementine Vulgate adds the gloss 'that is, Jehu son of Hanani the prophet' (hoc est, Jehu filium Hanani prophetam), stating that Baasha killed the prophet Jehu for delivering the message.
notes.16:9: The Vulgate reads 'horsemen' (equitum) rather than the Hebrew 'chariots', and condenses the Hebrew phrase 'who was over the house in Tirzah' into 'the prefect of Tirzah' (præfecti Thersa).
notes.16:28: Major textual addition in this Latin text: following Omri's death and Ahab's accession, material parallel to 1 Kings 22:46-49 concerning Jehoshaphat (whose name appears midway through the addition, with 'Asa his father' signaling the shift in subject) is inserted here, reflecting the Septuagint placement of the Jehoshaphat summary.
notes.16:34: The Vulgate's literal preposition 'in' (in Abiram ... in Segub) reflects the Hebrew idiom of price ('at the cost of'), fulfilling Joshua's curse on the rebuilder of Jericho (Joshua 6:26).
notes.17:1: The Vulgate preserves the Hebraistic elliptical oath formula 'Vivit Dominus... si erit...' (lit. 'The Lord... lives, if there will be dew and rain...'), which idiomatically expresses a solemn negation, and specifies plural 'words of my mouth' ('oris mei verba').
notes.17:13: Latin 'subcinericium panem parvulum' literally describes a small loaf baked under the ashes, paired with the diminutive 'farinula' ('little bit of flour').
notes.17:15: Where the Hebrew ends verse 15 with 'many days' and begins a new sentence in verse 16, the Vulgate closes verse 15 with 'et ex illa die' ('and from that day'), running the sentence directly into verse 16.
notes.17:20: Vulgate 'apud quam ego utcumque sustentor' ('with whom I am somehow sustained') is a distinctive rendering of the Hebrew phrase for sojourning with the widow.
notes.18:19: Vulgate 'lucorum' ('of the groves') is Jerome's standard rendering of Hebrew 'Asherah,' denoting sacred groves or cultic wooden poles.
notes.18:27: Vulgate 'in diversorio est' ('he is at an inn') is a distinctive rendering of Elijah's second taunt, where the Hebrew expression is often taken to mean stepping aside or relieving himself.
notes.18:32: Vulgate 'quasi per duas aratiunculas' ('about the space of two small furrows') expresses the trench size in terms of plowed furrows where the Hebrew speaks of a measure of two seahs of seed.
notes.18:44: Vulgate 'vestigium hominis' literally means 'a man's footprint' (reflecting Hebrew 'kaf,' which can denote either a palm or the sole of a foot), and narrates the sighting directly rather than as speech by the servant.
notes.18:45: Vulgate 'Cumque se verteret huc atque illuc' ('And as he turned this way and that') translates the Hebrew temporal idiom 'in a little while' (lit. 'until here and until here') as a physical turning.
notes.19:3: The Vulgate reads Timuit ("was afraid"), agreeing with the Septuagint against the Masoretic vocalization "saw," and renders Hebrew "for his life" as quocumque eum ferebat voluntas ("wherever his will carried him").
notes.19:12: Latin sibilus aurae tenuis ("a whisper of a light breeze") is a distinctive Vulgate rendering of the Hebrew phrase literally meaning "a sound of thin silence."
notes.19:18: The Vulgate specifies virorum ("men") and renders the Hebrew "has not kissed him" as non adoravit eum osculans manus ("has not worshiped him by kissing the hands"), reflecting the ancient gesture of homage toward idols.
notes.19:19: Latin in duodecim jugis boum arantibus unus erat ("was one among the twelve yokes of oxen that were plowing") differs from the Hebrew Masoretic Text, which states that Elisha was "with the twelfth."
notes.19:20: The Vulgate renders Elijah's reply as a declarative statement, quod enim meum erat, feci tibi ("for what was mine, I have done to you"), whereas the Hebrew has a rhetorical question ("for what have I done to you?").
notes.20:1: Following the chapter order of the Septuagint (3 Kingdoms), the Naboth's vineyard narrative appears here as chapter 20 rather than chapter 21 as in the Hebrew Masoretic Text and standard Sixto-Clementine Vulgate numbering.
notes.20:3: Latin Propitius sit mihi Dominus ("May the Lord be merciful to me") literally follows the Septuagint rendering of the Hebrew oath formula of refusal ("Far be it from me from the Lord").
notes.20:10: Latin Benedixit ("has blessed," also in 20:13) preserves literally the Hebrew pious euphemism for "cursed." The Vulgate transliterates filios Belial ("sons of Belial") here, but translates the same phrase in 20:13 as filiis diaboli ("sons of the devil") and viri diabolici ("diabolical men").
notes.20:21: Latin demetam posteriora tua ("I will cut down your posterity") uses a harvest metaphor for the Hebrew "sweep away after you," and clausum et ultimum ("the confined and the last") renders the Hebrew merism "bond and free."
notes.20:24: The Vulgate reads Si mortuus fuerit Achab ("If Ahab dies"), referring to Ahab himself rather than "anyone belonging to Ahab who dies" as in the Hebrew Masoretic Text; similarly, in 20:23 in agro Jezrahel ("in the field of Jezreel") contrasts with the Masoretic "rampart of Jezreel."
notes.21:6: Latin omne quod eis placuerit ("everything that pleases them," i.e., Ben-hadad's servants) aligns with the Septuagint and differs from the Hebrew Masoretic Text, which reads "whatever is desirable in your eyes."
notes.21:11: Latin accinctus ("girded/fastened") and discinctus ("ungirded/unfastened") are military terms referring to putting on and taking off a war-belt or armor before and after battle.
notes.21:34: In the Vulgate (et ego foederatus recedam a te), Ben-hadad continues speaking ("and I, bound by a treaty, will depart from you"), whereas in the Hebrew Masoretic Text Ahab speaks this clause ("and I will let you go with this treaty").
notes.21:38: Vulgate aspersione pulveris ("by a sprinkling of dust," continued in 21:41 abstersit pulverem, "wiped the dust") reflects reading the rare Hebrew word afer ("headband/bandage") as epher ("ashes/dust").
notes.21:43: Vulgate audire contemnens ("scorning to listen") renders the Hebrew adjective sar ("sullen" or "resentful") as stubborn refusal to heed the prophet's rebuke.
notes.22:24: The Vulgate renders Zedekiah's question as "Has the Spirit of the Lord then left me and spoken to you?" (Mene ergo dimisit spiritus Domini), whereas the Hebrew text asks which way the Spirit passed from him to speak to Micaiah.
notes.22:26: The Vulgate reads "let him remain with" (maneat apud) instead of the Hebrew "take him back to," and transliterates the Hebrew title hammelekh ("the king") as the proper name Amelech ("son of Amelech").
notes.22:30: The Vulgate has Ahab instruct Jehoshaphat in the second person ("Take up arms, and enter the battle"), whereas the Hebrew text has Ahab announce that he himself will disguise himself and enter the battle.
notes.22:34: The Vulgate translates the target of the arrow anatomically as "between the lung and the stomach" (inter pulmonem et stomachum) and adds "by chance" (casu), whereas the Hebrew refers to the gap between parts of the king's armor.
notes.22:38: The Vulgate renders this clause "and they washed the reins" (et habenas laverunt), taking the underlying Hebrew term as chariot harness or gear, whereas the Masoretic Hebrew reads "and the prostitutes washed themselves."
